iron-curtain.title: 🛡️ Iron Curtain: Part of the Recent Revival of Earth–Wind Hybrid
iron-curtain.description: A brand-new skill is coming to Infinity Kingdom, and it has the potential to shake up the meta in a big way. It’s called Iron Curtain, and while it’s not available just yet, early previews already have competitive players buzzing.
iron-curtain.html:
A brand-new skill is coming to Infinity Kingdom, and it has the potential to shake up the meta in a big way. It’s called Iron Curtain, and while it’s not available just yet, early previews already have competitive players buzzing.

At first glance, it may not look like a game-changer — but if you dig deeper, you’ll see why it could reshape defensive strategies and potentially bring back the Earth–Wind hybrid, one of the classic march archetypes that has fallen out of the spotlight.

⚔️ What Iron Curtain Does

Iron Curtain is a passive skill designed specifically for physical carries like Alexander, Poseidon, or Wukong. It has two distinct parts:

  1. Damage Reduction: When your troop count is above 70%, reduce damage taken by 35%.
    • This effectively makes your frontline much harder to burst down in the opening phase of a fight.
    • In today’s burst-heavy meta, surviving the first ultimate cycle often decides the match. Iron Curtain gives your frontliners a massive cushion, buying critical time.
  2. Barrier Weakening: When your normal attacks hit, there’s a 60% chance to weaken barriers on all enemies by 30% for 30 seconds.
    • The exact mechanics are still being clarified, while it is safe to assume it applies to shield like Charles’ ultimate and Energy Shield, we are still finding out if YSS shield effect for example are also part of this. If true, this could finally introduce a direct counter to YSS based meta teams.

🧩 Why This Matters

Part 1: The Early Damage Reduction

This is where the skill really shines.

  • With Iron Curtain, your physical carries take 35% less damage right at the start, which often means surviving with enough HP to keep swinging.
  • Survive longer = more attacks = more lifesteal/healing procs = higher total damage.

It can also be used for ramp-up strategies (like Battle Stance or Demonic Contract), which need time before hitting full power.

Part 2: Barrier Weakening

This is trickier. Shielding isn’t dominant in the current meta, so this effect won’t always be relevant. However:

  • If Iron Curtain counts all shielding effects (YSS’s protection, Charles’ shields, Energy Shield, Fu Fei, etc.), it becomes a flexible soft-counter.
  • Against Charles-heavy or tanky hybrid teams, reducing shield strength by 30% can absolutely matter.
  • Even if it’s niche right now, it future-proofs physical teams against any shift back toward shield-heavy metas.

🌪️ Why This Could Revive Earth–Wind Hybrid

For a long time, Earth–Wind hybrids were feared for their balance of tankiness and strong physical DPS. Then the burst meta pushed them out.

Iron Curtain changes the equation:

  • Add in the recent rise of auto-attack synergies (new normal attack procs, “Knife Through Butter” style skills), and suddenly Earth-Wind Hybrids are beginning to look viable again.

🏆 Who Should Use Iron Curtain?

  • Alexander –Gains survivability for one-on-one fights + benefits from high rate of auto-attacks for procs/triggers.
  • Poseidon – Becomes harder to delete early, possibly giving him time to ramp his AoE.
  • Any physical-heavy frontline looking to fight back against shield-setups.

🔮 Final Thoughts

Iron Curtain may not look flashy at first glance, but its 35% opening damage reduction alone is decent in today’s meta. Add in the potential of barrier weakening, and its adding up to be a nice skill. I do not think this will be overpowered in any way, and I dont see this as a default skill for every setup. But it is very good to hace an improved physical shield for alex that also counters charles-energy-shield builds. Very good, and a step towards brining back hybrids? Possibly!

👉 Expect to see Earth–Wind hybrids with Alexander and other physical carries re-enter the Conquest scene once Iron Curtain goes live. It’s not just a defensive skill — it’s a skill that could mark the start of a new meta cycle.

knife-through-butter.title: 🗡️ Knife Through Butter: The Energy-Shredder That Could Make the Next Version of Hybrid-builds
knife-through-butter.description: Infinity Kingdom’s next patch introduces one of the most disruptive Tower of Knowledge skills we’ve seen in years: Knife Through Butter. At first glance, its raw damage looks unremarkable — but its energy drain mechanic makes it potentially meta-breaking.
knife-through-butter.html:
Infinity Kingdom’s next patch introduces one of the most disruptive Tower of Knowledge skills we’ve seen in years: Knife Through Butter. At first glance, its raw damage looks unremarkable — but its energy drain mechanic makes it potentially meta-breaking.

This skill doesn’t just punish the current hyper-regen meta — it may also bring back the long-forgotten Earth–Wind hybrid archetype, putting physical carries like Alexander the Great back in the spotlight.

🔎 What Knife Through Butter Does

Skill Details:

  • Type: Physical, Attack-triggered
  • Effect: Normal attacks have a 60% chance to remove 300 Energy from all enemy Immortals
  • Proc Chance: 60% per 6 normal attack, thus scaling with attack speed.
  • Target: All enemies simultaneously

🚩 Why It’s a Big Deal

1. Hard Counter to Hyper-Regen Meta

Right now, many Conquest battles revolve around regen-based comps — teams that chain ultimates endlessly through energy boosts. These teams thrive on casting before you can react.

Knife Through Butter flips that on its head:

  • Every proc robs the entire enemy team of 300 energy.
  • With high attack speed, enemies may never reach ultimate thresholds.
  • Result: Heals, shields, and CC chains collapse.

2. Revival and evolution of Hybrid Teams

For several seasons, hybrids (earth wind) have struggled in the regen backline-centered meta. With Knife Through Butter, hybrids finally have a disruptive tool that rewards their natural strengths:

  • High attack speed carries like Alexander, Hannibal when boosted by Zeno and Qin for attack speed can proc this constantly.
  • By draining energy, they prevent enemy from cycling their devastating ultimates.
  • The freed-up space lets hybrids’ sustained DPS shine again.

The next evolution of Hybrid will be Alex-Ares frontline!?

In short: Hybrids get relevance back — not by brute force, but by shutting down the opponent’s key win condition. Perhaps even as a new version with Ares? I personally think so.

📊 Numbers That Matter

Let’s put the impact of Knife Through Butter into context, using a common hybrid setup:

  • Attack Speed Setup: With standard hybrid builds (e.g., Alexander running Wind Rage and Berserker), achieving 3-4 attacks per second is common in prolonged battles.
  • Proc Mechanics: With a 60% chance per 6 attacks attack, at 3 attacks per second, you average 1.8 procs per second (60% × 3 = .9 procs).
  • Energy Drain Impact: At each proc, you drain 300 Energy from each enemy Immortal. Averaging .9 procs per second gives us approximately 270 Energy drained per second from each enemy Immortal—an absolutely staggering number.

The idea is simple yet effective:

  • DPS #1 shuts down enemy ultimates by continuous energy drain.
  • DPS #2 quickly bursts down priority targets who become vulnerable due to interrupted heals, controls and shields.

🎯 How It Fits Into Conquest Meta

Hybrid Resurgence

  • Earth–Wind hybrids with Alexander and Hannibal suddenly look dangerous again.
  • With Knife Through Butter, they can suppress backline enery regen based builds that otherwise ramping up damage.

More Attack-Speed Builds

  • Expect Wind Rage, Berserker, and other speed-enhancers to become mandatory.

Whale Must-Have

  • For spenders, this skill will likely be required for top Conquest matches.
  • Any team without energy control will risk being steamrolled by Knife Through Butter comps.

Implications

  • Skills like Energy Suppression may see renewed relevance as synergies to constant energy drain.
  • Teams that rely less on ultimate cycles (like raw crit Khan comps) will adapt faster.

🏆 Final Thoughts

Knife Through Butter isn’t just another skill — it’s a meta-shifter. By introducing large-scale energy disruption, it dismantles regen-based setups and opens the door for hybrid physical builds to thrive again.

  • For Whales: It’s almost mandatory. If you want to compete at the very top, you’ll need it.
  • For Mid-Spenders: It’s a ticket to punch above your weight, especially in Conquest battlegroups dominated by regen comps.
  • For the Meta: Expect hybrid marches (Alex-Hannibal earth wind) to climb back to the top.

⚡ Verdict: This is a very interesting skill and one that in the right build may be the most broken energy skill so far? Right now it looks strong but not broken, but I think that once whales figure out how to setup Alexander-Ares hybrids, we are going to see some new top builds and a new hybrid era… time will tell!

abundant-spirit.title: Abundant Spirit
abundant-spirit.description: Abundant Spirit is one of those skills that doesn’t look insane at first glance… until you actually run it on a mage march that already stacks multiple triggered ToK skills. Then it suddenly feels like you unlocked an extra gear your team didn’t have before.
abundant-spirit.html:
Abundant Spirit is one of those skills that doesn’t look insane at first glance… until you actually run it on a mage march that already stacks multiple triggered ToK skills. Then it suddenly feels like you unlocked an extra gear your team didn’t have before.

The big catch, though? It’s not a normal Tower of Knowledge skill. It’s locked behind Ability Selection Chest I (with the most expensive skills in the game equal to 2x full legendary skills) however, lucky for you this skill is also available for FREE in the Legion of Frostborne from conquest P1 and onwards. In essence, NEVER waste a selection Chest I on this skill as it is literally F2P from KvK rewards.

Once you get your hands on it, though, it becomes one of the cleanest power spikes you can give a mage immortal—but only when you run it correctly.

Skill Breakdown

Abundant Spirit
“Upon entering battle, increases the triggering probability of your skills by 10% and Magic Damage by 30%.”

Two parts here:

1. +30% Magic Damage

This is basically a second Concentration. Anyone who has played mages for a while knows Concentration has been a staple forever, so getting another Concentration-tier buff in the same slot category is already strong.

2. +10% Trigger Chance for your SKILLS

And this is where people mess up.

The skill says “your skills,” and that only refers to Tower of Knowledge triggered skills, not immortal ultimate abilities.

So:

  • Works on: Annihilation, Chase, Infinite Firepower, Heavy Lifter, Poison Thorn, Spell Disintegrator, etc.
  • Does NOT work on: Wu’s multi-hit ultimate, Baldwins’s extra explosions, etc.

If it’s from the Tower of Knowledge, it gets buffed. If it’s an immortal’s ultimate, it does not get buffed.

This is important because if you run Abundant Spirit without other triggered ToK skills, you’re basically wasting half the value.

How It Actually Performs in Battles

This is where the skill starts to feel absurd. Since it increases the trigger probability, you’re not just hitting harder—you’re hitting more often. When you combine the two, your burst windows go crazy.

A good example from live testing:

  • Annihilation has a 45% trigger rate.
  • With Abundant Spirit, that jumps to 55%.
  • That’s roughly a 22% damage increase just for Annihilation on average (because extra triggers scale with the 30% magic damage boost too).

When you stack two triggered skills, the effect multiplies – For example in a Spell Disintegration + Chase build.

Abundant Spirit looks like a magic damage skill, but it’s actually a trigger engine.
If you want to get real value from it, you MUST pair it with multiple trigger-based ToK skills.

These are the usual suspects:

  • Annihilation – still the king of burst, becomes noticeably more consistent
  • Infinite Firepower – extra triggers = extra burn cycles
  • Heavy Lifter – surprisingly strong when trigger rate climbs
  • Poison Thorn – works fine, very consistent
  • Spell Disintegrator – this is the one that went insane in testing

The trick is that Abundant Spirit doesn’t add value in a vacuum. It amplifies whatever trigger-based kit you build around it.

Best Immortals to Run It On

Pretty straightforward: anyone who is a primary magic damage dealer and you are doing a build that relies on chance-trigger skills. Such as a chase-trigger build or just a build with annihilation and spell disintegration / IF / etc.

Wu and Himiko especially love it because they run extremely well with multi-trigger setups. Baldwin benefits a ton too because he’s already burst-heavy. Merlin can run it but feels slightly more mid-game dependent unless you build him aggressively for burst.

Where It Shines Most

On immortals that:

  1. Already scale from magic damage buffs
  2. Already have strong triggered ToK setups
  3. Stay alive long enough to let their skills fire repeatedly

Wu is probably the most “immediate” fit—fire marches already love stacking ToK damage skills and doing chase builds. Problem however is you are replacing a slot which could be a Chase trigger in itself – or the more crucial Fighting Master slot which any Wu fire build short of a Fu Fei fire must be running against the mass control of immortals and builds these days. That makes this imo. a decent spell but not something meta defining. Personally, I am going to out it to use in my second team where it will be with SD and Anni on a Baldwin mage.

Conclusion Summary

Abundant Spirit is basically Concentration 2.0 with a built-in trigger engine. It’s locked behind expensive chests, but if you get it, it becomes one of the strongest mage-oriented skills in the game as long as you pair it with other triggered ToK skills.

What you get from it:

  • A flat +30% magic damage buff (always good)
  • +10% trigger chance on ALL ToK triggered skills
  • Adds consistency to RNG spikes in burst damage
  • Synergy with meta mages like Wu and Himiko

Bottom line:
If you’re building a serious mage march and you can stack multiple triggered skills, Abundant Spirit is a great option. It is a powerful damage booster in itself and the reduction of RNG reliance in favor of more consistent and much higher skill damage output, is very good! Many mages will see their tower of knowledge skills being close to as much damage as their ultimates, and with this skill we are boosting the damage of ults, and skills as well as increasing the consistency and damage of skills even further through increased trigger chance. Very cool and a skill I am very glad that they have added. Giving options to smoothen out gameplay and reduce RNG is always something that I am in favor of.

energy-master.html:
Introduction

Energy Master is one of the most influential Legendary skills in Infinity Kingdom, and it has reshaped how backline carries function in Conquest. When you run a mage or bowman with Energy Master, you always want to pair that carry with a support immortal running Battle Excitation. This pairing is the engine behind the modern ultimate-cycling meta: the support accelerates the initial energy curve, and Energy Master ensures the backline carry never slows down once casting begins.

The result is a dramatic shift away from older double-healer or bruiser-carry setups. In Conquest, the defining hallmark of a competitive march is a backline damage dealer whose ultimate fires rapidly and repeatedly, supported by both talents and skills designed to maintain that cycle.

Let’s break down how Energy Master accomplishes this.

1. What Energy Master Does and Why It’s Meta-Defining

Energy Master provides:

  • A large instant energy refund every time the immortal casts an ultimate.
  • A significant energy-skill damage increase for several seconds after each cast.
  • A cast rhythm that becomes progressively faster as the battle continues.

Together, these effects do far more than increase damage:
Energy Master changes the entire pace of a fight. It frontloads enormous burst damage while pushing cast frequency far beyond what older builds could achieve. Instead of waiting for the typical ramp-up to full energy, your carry enters a loop where ultimates are fired in rapid succession, and each cast fuels the next. This extremely compressed damage window is what has defined the meta in the Conquest era.

2. Energy Master and the Ultimate-Cycling Engine

2.1 How the Core Loop Works

The typical structure is:

  • Backline carry (mage or archer) → has Energy Master.
  • Backline support → runs Battle Excitation talents to boost initial energy.
  • Frontline tanks/supports → stabilize the fight and create time for the carry to cycle.

You can also run Rage Blessing on a tank or support.
Rage Blessing provides a 3/4 chance to grant your team additional energy regeneration, and in practice, this often lands on your carry. When it does, it accelerates the cycle even further, reinforcing the Energy Master engine.

2.2 What This Looks Like in Combat

Once the carry fires the first ultimate:

  • Energy Master immediately refunds a large portion of the bar.
  • If you pair it with Corrosive Power, you add drip-feed energy on damage ticks.
  • Battle Excitation and Rage Blessing smooth the regen between casts.

See the energy of Himiko on the right side, her energy is being refunded as she casts and as she deals damage in this video. This is ult-cycling using Energy Master and Corrosive Power.

You no longer watch your carry drop to low energy and slowly climb back up. Instead, ultimates appear rapidly, one after another, and opponents take heavy burst damage before they’ve fully ramped themselves.

This produces dramatically higher total damage, but more importantly, far more rapid damage output, because the team avoids the slow buildup that used to define earlier seasons.

3. Comparing Energy Master to Psionic Tide and Corrosive Power

3.1 Psionic Tide

  • Strong energy regeneration skill.
  • Outclassed by Energy Master for primary carries. Energy Master (EM) provides double the energy refund. For Mages specifically, Psionic Tide does bring a strong damage buff with it affecting your Tower of Knowledge skills damage as well as your own by 15% stacking 3 times. But for ultimate-cycling, the 100% Energy skill damage buff from EM is superior as well.
  • Note Psionic cannot be equipped together with Energy Master. If you are using Energy Master in your main or on a ranged-carry, Psionic can be substitute for a mage, but for mains EM is superior.

Energy Master simply drives ultimates harder and faster, and its damage window is substantially stronger.

3.2 Corrosive Power

  • Excellent synergy skill.
  • Adds ultimate damage and continuous energy gains on hit.
  • Can be paired with Energy Master (or Psionic for that matter), which is currently one of the highest-performing carry combinations in the game.

For burst-centric carries, Energy Master + Corrosive Power defines the current gold-standard build.

Note: After the most recent nerf to Seondeok, her trigger effects on her ultimate no longer counts as ultimate damage, hence you cannot get the buffs and regen from e.g. an EM+Corrosive combination that you used to. That makes Corrosive Power near useless on her specifically, but Energy Master does still work well here.

4. Supporting Skills and Talents

4.1 Battle Excitation (Support Only)

Battle Excitation is exclusive to support immortals, and in the Energy Master meta it is mandatory. It significantly improves the opening of the fight by boosting initial energy, which allows your carry to reach the first ultimate more quickly. Without that acceleration, the Energy Master engine still works, but it loses much of its sharpness.

4.2 Rage Blessing on Tanks/Supports

Rage Blessing adds a probabilistic layer of additional energy regeneration. When its 3/4 chance lands on your carry—and it often does—it further tightens the cycle and compounds the value of Energy Master, especially in long fights. While this does NOT affect refuned energy from Energy Master (or other sources) it does provide synergy to the general concept of ultimate-cycling builds.

4.3 Owl Guardian Talents

Running an energy centric build, you should make sure to always be using the Owl Guardian Talents, providing a 5% buff to the passive energy regen of your immortals. While this does NOT affect refuned energy from Energy Master (or other sources) it does provide synergy to the general concept of ultimate-cycling builds.

5. Best Immortals for Energy Master

Any primary damage dealer that relies on ultimate damage burst hits performs extremely well with Energy Master. It is not limited to AoE casters; single-target burst or multi-hit patterns also scale beautifully.

5.1 Mages

  • Himiko
    Balanced, consistent, and extremely reliable. Energy Master elevates her damage curve and ensures fast casting cycles.
  • Baldwin
    Higher theoretical output than Himiko but more RNG-dependent. With Energy Master, his peaks become devastating, though you still experience the occasional low-roll battle.
  • Merlin, Empress Wu, Hammurabi, others
    Any mage built around strong ultimate bursts benefits greatly from Energy Master + regen builds.

5.2 Archers

  • Genghis Khan
    High crit synergy and excellent scaling with rapid ultimates. Strong Energy Master pairing.
  • Apollo
    Absolutely not a niche pick—Apollo becomes a very strong primary carry with Energy Master. His kit aligns tightly with fast-cycling builds, making him one of the more promising long-term archer carries in Conquest.

6. Leveling Priority & Investment Advice

Energy Master does not require max level to outperform other skills.
However, instead of feeling powerful at level 2–4, the practical threshold where it begins clearly surpassing most alternatives is around level 5.

  • Level 5: The energy refund becomes large enough to sustain a reliable cycle.
  • Level 6–7: The higher the level the better, that being said, at the 6-7 range we are getting to levels that makes the skill unrivaled by anything else on many burst-immortals.
  • Level 8?: Yes, you want to get this to level 8 if possible. That being said, due to the nature of how the required skill stones to upgrade each level increases, most players find it the most effective to end upgrading at level 7 and move on to the next legendary skill – then to return once you have the ones you need at their appropriate levels.

Upgrade costs to Chaos/Legendary Skills:

Unlock: 60
level 2: 5
level 3: 10
level 4: 15
level 5: 20
level 6: 30
level 7: 40
level 8: 60
Total 240

For players investing in Legendary skills, Energy Master is typically the best first choice for any account built around a backline carry.

Conclusion

Energy Master is not just a high-damage Legendary skill; it is the foundation of the current ultimate-cycling meta. When paired with a support that has Battle Excitation, and supported further by skills like Rage Blessing and Corrosive Power, it creates a fight rhythm defined by:

  • extremely rapid ultimate frequency,
  • compressed burst windows,
  • and total damage outputs far beyond the older Season 2 meta.

Any backline carry built around ultimate burst gains exceptional value from it. Whether you’re running Himiko, Baldwin, Merlin, Wu, Khan, or Apollo, Energy Master transforms them from strong damage dealers into game-defining ones.

fully-prepared.title: Fully Prepared – The perfect Alexander / Ares skill
fully-prepared.description: Fully Prepared: The Rise of Momentum-Based Defense in Infinity Kingdom
fully-prepared.html:
Fully Prepared: The Rise of Momentum-Based Defense in Infinity Kingdom

Introduction – Momentum as a Front-Line Philosophy

Legendary passive skills in Infinity Kingdom usually force a choice between damage and survival. Fully Prepared breaks that pattern. It offers a unified design built around momentum: keep attacking, grow stronger, take less damage. No HP thresholds. No emergency triggers. Just steady pressure rewarded over time.

In a meta where we have in the past often seen conditional passives like Last Stand or Iron Curtain, Fully Prepared represents a philosophical shift. Instead of reacting to danger, it assumes control from the first strike. The skill asks one thing of the player and the immortal alike—maintain rhythm. As long as normal attacks continue, both offense and defense scale upward in tandem.

This is not something that requires you to maintain high troop counts to even work, nor does it assume you loose 30% of your troops before it even takes effect. Instead it is a commitment to tempo and to getting ahead fast and then staying ahead. And that pays off!

Skill Overview – How Fully Prepared Functions

Fully Prepared is a Legendary Passive Skill restricted to front-line positions.

Each normal attack grants two stacking effects:

  • Damage dealt increased by a fixed percentage per hit
  • Damage taken reduced by a fixed percentage per hit

These effects stack up to 10 times. At higher skill levels, the scaling becomes substantial.

At level 8, each stack provides:

  • +6% damage dealt
  • −5% damage taken

At full stacks, this results in:

  • +60% total damage
  • −50% total damage taken

The moment normal attacks stop, the momentum ends. Stacks do not persist through inactivity or control effects.

Fully Prepared cannot be equipped alongside Last Stand or Iron Curtain, as all three occupy the same defensive design space. Where those skills rely on conditional triggers, Fully Prepared replaces them with cumulative scaling tied directly to combat flow.

Damage Scaling – Power Earned Through Persistence

The offensive value of Fully Prepared is easy to underestimate at first glance. In practice, it competes directly with – and often outperforms – traditional damage passives.

At maximum level, Fully Prepared reaches +60% damage, matching Last Stand’s peak bonus. The difference lies in uptime.

Last Stand only activates once HP drops below a specific threshold. Fully Prepared begins scaling from the opening exchange. On fast-attacking front liners, full stacks are typically reached within the first 8-10 seconds of combat.

This creates a form of compounding pressure:

  • Early stacks accelerate mid-fight damage
  • Mid-fight damage shortens engagements
  • Shorter engagements reduce incoming risk

Rather than gambling on survival to unlock damage, Fully Prepared front-loads value and maintains it as long as attacks continue. In extended fights, that consistency translates into cleaner victories and fewer collapses.

Durability and Mitigation – Proactive, Not Reactive

The defensive side of Fully Prepared is where its design truly stands apart.

At full stacks, 50% damage reduction exceeds Iron Curtain’s maximum mitigation and does so without waiting for a trigger window or conditional triggers from e.g. troop counts. Protection builds quickly (especially on high speed normal attackers) as combat progresses.

This reframes the role of front-line immortals. Instead of functioning purely as damage sponges, they become damage regulators—reducing incoming pressure while actively accelerating the enemy’s defeat.

The tradeoff is clear and deliberate: momentum can be broken.

  • Stuns, knockbacks, or forced downtime interrupt stacking
  • Lost stacks mean lost mitigation
  • Recovery requires re-establishing attack rhythm

Because of this, Fully Prepared strongly favors builds that minimize interruption through control resistance, immunity, or sheer attack speed. When uninterrupted, the skill delivers some of the most stable frontline durability available.

Ideal Users and Synergies – Where Fully Prepared Excels

Fully Prepared shines on immortals who stay in contact and attack frequently. It is strongest on aggressive front lines designed for prolonged engagement rather than burst windows.

Recommended Immortals

  • Alexander – One of the most natural fits. His rapid attack chains allow stacks to build almost immediately, and his control immunity protects momentum. Perfect fit.
  • Ares – Blends aggression with his Frigthen utility, quick normal attacks, making full-stack uptime reliable in drawn-out fights (as of the coming patch 2.9.0 Ares will also have a baked in Control Immunity perfect for maintaining momentum and uptime).
  • Hannibal Barca – Slower to ramp but benefits heavily from long exchanges where stacks remain stable. Requires Fighting Master as to attain Control Immunity, since this takes up a skill slot he is significantly worse off than Ares (once patch 2.9.0 is live) and Alex where you are able to run both Wind Rage and Knife Through Butter, more on that below.

Skill Synergies

  • Wind Rage – The single most important pairing. This skill provides a huge increase to the number of normal attacks you land per second. Hence it significantly reduces stack buildup time.
  • Knife Through Butter – Complements the scaling damage by maintaining pressure throughout the fight and by also scaling off of normal attack, making it a perfect synergy with Wind Rage which we want to run with Fully Prepared.
  • Assembly Charge – Works well in aggressive dual-front setups that commit to sustained combat. Also scales off of normal attacks, hence works in synergy with the Wind Rage core. In my opinion, Assembly Charge is the skill to get if you do not have a Knife Through Butter level 6-8 available.

The perfect setup is in my opinion doing Wind Rage with Fully Prepared and Knife Through Butter – as shown below.

Obtaining Fully Prepared

Fully Prepared is a Legendary skill, meaning it is available only through the Wisdom Well event in Conquest and Legendary seasons. Being a legendary skill, you need additional skill stones to upgrade Fully Prepared – contrary to Epic skills which we are used to upgrading using Soul Crystals.

The cost to unlock is 60 skill stones, upgrading each level gets more and more expensive for a total of 240 stones required to reach level 8. Note that because level 7 to 8 costs a whopping 60 skill stones in itself, many players opt to stay at level 6 or 7 for a while and being upgrading other skills – then returning once you complete your legendary skill loadout. This is my recommendation as you progress into legendary skill setups as well.

Upgrade costs to Chaos/Legendary Skills:
Unlock: 60
level 2: 5
level 3: 10
level 4: 15
level 5: 20
level 6: 30
level 7: 40
level 8: 60
Total 240

Conclusion – The Backbone of Sustained Combat

Fully Prepared does not rescue failing positions. It amplifies strong ones.

When used correctly, it turns steady aggression into both offense and defense, scaling power through discipline rather than desperation. For players who value tempo, uptime, and sustained control, it stands as one of the most coherent and rewarding passive designs in the game.

tok-aura-tier-list.html:
This article is part of my section on passives (ToK skills). Passives are the most important thing to understand in IK if you want to craft a strong march setup and win the many battles ahead. They are extreemly powerful and makes a huge difference in a fight. A strong well thoughtout setup can beat enemies with FAR superior power numbers with ease. Passives are what defines the meta and you should spend a long time studying the effects and the many options available if you are an ambitious player.

It is through (1) Immortal compositions and (2) passive setup that you can craft counter marches.

This article will dive into the AURA passives available in the Tower of Knowledge (ToK). I will explain every aura and how it works, and how you need to think about the aura when creating setups with them. I will also link to some usecases for each aura to explain the rationale behind the passive.

It is recommended to always have 2 auras in your setup. Though only very rarely should you have 3 or 4.

Aura Tier List

S-tier

Malice, Weakness and Coercion are all S-tier auras. This is simply because these are the three auras with the absolute highest impact in the game. Crits are hugely important in IK, as critical hits are sometimes avg. 3-4 times a normal attack (even at low tech). Therefore, using Malice and Weakness are the two best auras for 99% of all setups you can make. You will never go wrong setting both of them in your main – even if your team is not crit-reliant as in running chase-synergies or Cyrus. You will still see very high impact from both these crit-auras.

Coercion is somewhere in between S and A tier. Simply because, not every march / setup relies on physical damage. For physical damage Immortals, accuracy is the most valuable stat you can get. A miss/dodged attack is a 100% damage reduction, and as such even a small amout of misses means you are missing out on a lot of DPS. If you rely on physical damage from e.g. Alexander + Bathony or Barca + Saladin + Atalanta or YSG + Peter + Khan you MUST have coercion. However, for someone relying on big damage spells, coercion is absolutely pointless, your auto attacks on mages are very small and magic skills cannot miss. Because it is a must have for physical damage dealers, I cannot get myself to set it as a A-tier skill. But note that it shouldn’t be used on magic setups. If you run 2-3 physical damage dealers in your march, it is mostly recommended to run all three of these auras. Only in some niche occations you need to do otherwise (see below).

A-tier

Shelter and Berserk are both A-tier auras. These two auras are ranked highly, as they are both high impact and versatile auras. They provide sustain (and Berserk attack speed) which is very strong for both PvE and PvP combat. This makes them some of the most valuable ToK skills to unlock.

Beware, that in PvP situations where you are faced with an enemy with “wounds” debuff. The value of these auras drop hard. In any other situation, they provide very strong sustain to your march and are always a good choice.

Berserk synergizes especially well with Immortals which scale off of attack speed (i.e. Immortals like Hannibal Barca and Alexander the Great).

B-Tier

Sacrifice and Missleading I have ranked as B-tier, i.e. situational auras. These are the auras I rarely use and only in specific situations / setups.

Missleading is situational very solid in a setup with other means of sustaining itself, made to fight versus physical damage immortals. Since hit-rate is the most valuable stat for a physical damage dealing immortal, adding to your dodge chance can be a huge factor when fighting physical damage dealers. However, this aura is countered quite hard by coercion, making its value quite low versus enemies with coercion IF you do not stack it with anything else. As such, I personally run it in my third march because I run holy with Manco and Afterimage too. Making my dodge a real factor of survival and ‘overcapping’ on dodge to make coercion not able to saturate the deficit imposed on enemy hit chance.

Sacrifice is a decent aura, on paper it is insanely strong. But I do not like it when running 2 supports and 2 damage dealers (which is most setups). Sacrifice is valuable in situations where you have a support Immortal with 0 damage output AND have 3 other Immortals all with decent damage output. This could e.g. be Dido, Merlin, Ragnar, Attila.

C-Tier

I cannot get myself to set any of the auras as less than decent. Every aura available in the game has a high impact relative to most of the other ToK passive skills. As such, the lowest ranked aura Paralysis is ranked as decent.

Paralysis is a decent aura in that it provides a bit of a slowdown on enemy autoattacks. This creates a slight damage output reduction for any enemy you face, yet it is a lot more impactful in highly specific encounters. Basically, I only like Paralysis when fighting against: Alexander, Barca, Attila and Peter. Yet even against these opponents I would ALWAYS prioritize one of the above auras. Paralysis works nicely in your second or third march, IF you are going for sustain / defense versus auto-attack (white hit) Immortals.

passive-skill-combos.title: Passive Skill Combos / strategies
passive-skill-combos.description: ToK Skills are the Tower of Knowledge skills you can buy for Soul Crystals in the game to enhance your marches’ DPS, Control or Sustain, as well as to grant some special effects.
passive-skill-combos.html:
ToK Skills are the Tower of Knowledge skills you can buy for Soul Crystals in the game to enhance your marches’ DPS, Control or Sustain, as well as to grant some special effects.

Asking for what is the best blessing or aura on a specific immortal wouldn’t be the correct quesiton. Instead, you should ask what are your team’s strengths and vulnerabilities so you know what auras and blessings best fit your team as a whole.

As an example, Fire has a very strong DPS while being very vulnerable to physical damage. That way, you can push this strength by adding Weakness(increases crit), while adding Oaken(reduces physical damage taken) and Misleading(increases your dodge) to protect you against Physical damage.

In addition, you have to think about how the elemental dragon interacts with ToK skills. For example, the fire dragon scales damage from buff = blessings gain increased value for fire teams. Same with debuffs for Lightning.

You can think about your teams vulnerabilities but some of the best combos are:

For blessings

  • Oaken + Resist: Strong protection for 18s, so it’s the safest option when it comes to blessings.
  • Rage Bless + Energy Suppression: Useful at getting first hits on enemies, meaning they don’t get to do as much damage back to you. Take into account this combo doesn’t work properly for fire*.
  • Oaken + Energy Suppression: Uses the best sides of each of the skills above. Useful for delaying Khan from casting his skill before your Water dragon heals.
  • War Bless + Defense Blesss: More useful for second or third marches, but still a good combo.

For Auras, you can choose 2 to 4 of the following:

  • Malice is such a powerful defensive skill for it’s reduction in crit rates by 20% for the enemy, which basically means you take around 20% less damage. Almost a must have skill for a main team.
  • Weakness: Like Malice but offensive. You buff your crit rate by 20%, so very usefull for any team and a must have for fire or teams that want to use Energy Burst or Chase.
  • Misleading: Increasing your Dodge by 20% means a big reduction in enemy DPS, but also soft-counters Crowd Control(CC) effects like Attila’s silence, as you can dodge 20% of his ultimates.
  • Coercion: Can be used in any team but it is a must have skill on teams that have no mages, such as Lightning and Holy. Not using this skill would make you very vulnerable against Misleading users.
  • Shelter: Very strong healing in a single aura. It is best used in sustain marches like Earth, as the value there only increases as the fight prolongues.
  • Sacrifice: This is a mini version of Weakness. Buffing the DPS of 2 immortals by 15% is still solid and worthy using on second marches.
  • Berserk: Not the best aura but this skill brings some healing and attack speed, so it’s best used in Earth or Wind, since both benefit a lot from increased attack speed.

The most noteworthy combinations you need to know about

The skills availble in the Tower of Knowledge, have a very high variety in terms of effect. While most skills revolve around damage and protection many are more utalitarian and can be used to create powerful combinations. We have tanky skills like Absolute Defense, some give tanks offense ability such as Life Link. Others provide control immunities, i.e. Fighting Master and we have Duel Master, that bring protecting against anti-heal effects.

1. Adrenaline Rush(AR) is great on frontline immortals who have very strong Ultimate Skills and low innate Energy Regen(ER). So it goes great on Charles, William, Saladin, Peter and Attila.

2. Energy Burst(EB) is equivalent to AR but made for backline immortals or immortals with high crit rate. Since Damage over Time(DoT) skills can actually crit, this skill is very well used on Gilgamesh and Elizabeth. But also does very well on the immortals with highest crit in the game: mages(not so good on Wu tho, her natural energy regen is too high already).

Just make sure you are using Death Breath or other high hit rate skills such as Cleave, Nova or Chaotic Blade for the number of crits to be even higher. Other honorable mentions of immortals that go well with EB would be Hippolyta and William, since fire has such high crit rate.

3. Demon Body is an underrated skill. I would call it a mini-Khan, as it bring an anti-heal effect around 1/3 as good as Khan’s.

4. Silence is another underrated skill. It is a mini-Attila! And very good investment early on, as it is a blue skill, only falling behind other stronger skills at the late game.

5. Root is the last of the extreemly underated skills I will mention. It often rivals fire nova / toxic nova in damage and provides more control than Richard!

6. Duel Master is a weaker version of Anger, but brings you immunity to anti-heal, so you could use it on heal based teams.

7. Absolute Defense(AD) is the best defensive skill for backline immortals, as it allows our squishy backlines to negative huge amounts of damage. This skill is very RNG based and needs to be at a high level to be consistent enough

8. Life Link(LL) is a hybrid skill, since it reduces incoming damage while dealing damage back to the enemy. It can be used on any frontline immortal and is best used on Sustain based teams, since healing means you can take and reflect more damage.

9. Fighting Will(FW) does some damage but it’s main use is to root the enemy, disabling them from doing normal attacks and casting ToK skills. A very strong skill in any team, but, again, best used in teams that posses healing, since you can recharge it’s uses.

10. Fighting Master(FM) is great on Crowd Control immortals or mages. The idea is FM is used to protect skills of big value from getting stunned or silenced. So it can be used on Attila, Hippo, Charles or any Mages… to protect their Ultimate skills, and preferably let it protect other big value skills like Annihilation, Fighting Will and Assist.

11. Speaking of Assist, this is one of the best skills in the game. Instead of having multiple immortals carrying Damage skills, this skill allows you to condese all DPS skills on one or two immortals, while the rest of the team focuses on keeping them alive!

There are two main ways of using assist:

  • You can use it on a frontline immortal, by running Assist+FW/LL/FM.
  • Or, you can have it on your Range/Support immortal, by running Assist+AD/FW/LL/FM.

All of these 2 skill combos meantioned are viable. It is recommended to leave the 3rd skill slot for an aura.

Special thank you to Mr. Harddus for providing most of the information above! <3

normal-attack-skills.html:
Mastering Infinity Kingdom: Unleashing Skills Based on Normal Attacks

When it comes to conquering the vast realms of Infinity Kingdom, understanding your heroes’ skills and how to use them effectively can make all the difference in your journey. In this guide, we’ll delve into the art of utilizing skills based on normal attacks, focusing on some of the most potent abilities in the game.

1. Combo, Cleave, and Heavenly Thunder

These skills are the bread and butter for many Infinity Kingdom heroes, including the likes of Alex. What makes them so appealing is their reliance on normal attacks, making them perfect for heroes with high attack speed. Alex, with his rapid strikes, is a prime example. When these skills proc, they can wreak havoc on the battlefield. Moreover, heroes like Alex can further amplify their effectiveness by investing in increased attack damage, turning these skills into devastating weapons.

2. Wind Rage

Wind Rage is a skill that truly shines when paired with heroes like Alex or Hannibal, or even immortals running Adrenaline Rush. The key to its power lies in its synergy with other skills such as Combo and Cleave. By combining Wind Rage with these skills, you can unleash a whirlwind of destruction upon your foes. It’s like a storm of blades, tearing through enemy ranks and leaving chaos in its wake.

3. Battle Stance

Battle Stance is a skill that benefits heroes like Alex and Hannibal, especially when they are immortals. At the beginning of a battle, it grants immortality, ensuring your hero’s survival in the early stages. However, the real kicker comes when Oaken Guard, your opponent’s protective shield, runs out. At that point, Battle Stance doubles your damage output, turning your hero into a formidable force to be reckoned with. It’s all about patience and timing.

4. Berserker

Much like Wind Rage, the Berserker skill finds its ideal partners in heroes like Alex and Hannibal. This skill reaches its full potential when combined with other normal attack-based abilities such as Wind Fury, Combo, and Cleave. When activated, Berserker elevates your hero’s damage output to unimaginable heights, turning them into an unstoppable juggernaut. It’s a frenzy of attacks that can break through even the toughest defenses.

5. Absorb

Absorb is a skill designed for heroes like Alex or Hannibal, who boast a high normal attack damage output. It’s a skill that not only deals damage but also ensures the hero’s survival on the battlefield. When paired with Duel Master, Absorb becomes even more potent. Not only does it heal your hero, but it also increases the damage dealt, creating a synergy that can turn the tide of battle in your favor. It’s a combination of offense and defense, making your hero an unyielding force.

In conclusion, mastering the skills based on normal attacks in Infinity Kingdom is all about understanding your heroes, their strengths, and their synergies with other abilities. Whether you’re raining down blows with Combo and Cleave, unleashing the fury of Wind Rage, adopting the strategic Battle Stance, going berserk with Berserker, or absorbing damage with Absorb, these skills can be the keys to victory in your conquest of the Infinity Kingdom. So, assemble your heroes, refine your strategies, and let your normal attacks pave the way to glory!

safeguarding-single-immortals.description: Fortify and Protect: Skills for Safeguarding Single Immortals
safeguarding-single-immortals.html:
Fortify and Protect: Skills for Safeguarding Single Immortals

In the vast and unpredictable world of Infinity Kingdom, safeguarding your single immortals is often a strategic necessity. Understanding the skills that can shield these heroes from harm can be the key to victory. In this guide, we’ll explore the skills designed to protect single immortals and the heroes who benefit most from them.

1. Fighting Master

Fighting Master is a skill that finds its true calling with key frontline immortals who have low energy regeneration rates, such as Charles or Hannibal (in hybrid formations). These heroes are formidable on the battlefield but are vulnerable to interruptions, especially from Earth Dragons or frontline cavalry immortals like those with Lance Thrust. Fighting Master becomes especially efficient when combined with Adrenaline Rush, as it can help prevent constant energy regeneration interruptions.

By equipping your frontline heroes with Fighting Master, you can ensure that they continue to deliver devastating blows without the risk of being interrupted. This skill allows them to maintain their offensive prowess, even in the face of relentless enemies.

2. Physical Shield

Physical Shield is a skill tailored for frontline DPS heroes like Manco, Siegfried, and Hannibal. Frontline immortals typically boast high HP pools, making additional damage reduction particularly effective for them. This added durability goes a long way in prolonging their presence on the battlefield, allowing them to withstand enemy attacks.

Since all auto attacks in the game deal physical damage, frontline heroes endure more physical pressure than their backline counterparts. Equipping them with Physical Shield can significantly enhance their survivability, making them sturdy bulwarks against enemy assaults.

3. Life Link

Life Link is a skill that provides additional damage reduction, making it ideal for frontline DPS heroes like Manco, Siegfried, and Hannibal or frontline heroes that use Assist. Just like with Physical Shield, this skill benefits from the high HP of frontline immortals, as the additional damage reduction goes a long way in keeping them alive.

Frontline heroes face more pressure from enemy auto attacks, which makes Life Link even more effective in redirecting damage away from them. This skill pairs exceptionally well with Assist or Guard, although it’s worth noting that it may not be a perfect fit for all immortals who benefit from Life Link.

4. Void Realm

Void Realm is a skill designed for support immortals or those who don’t primarily deal damage, such as Tomyris, Dido, or Matilda. This skill’s effectiveness is magnified when used in combination with Assist. By deploying Void Realm on your support immortals, you ensure that they remain safe and protected while assisting their allies on the battlefield.

5. Absolute Defense

Absolute Defense is an invaluable skill that can make a world of difference in safeguarding a single Immortal on the battlefield. This remarkable ability completely blocks incoming attacks, providing an impenetrable shield against harm. What sets Absolute Defense apart is its high activation rate, making it a dependable choice for Immortals engaged in prolonged battles.

It’s important to note that troop count plays a pivotal role in enhancing the effectiveness of healers. Therefore, if you have a backline Immortal healer or a damage support unit, combining Absolute Defense with their skill set can create a formidable defense. This combination ensures not only their survival but also the continued support they can offer to your team.

Incorporating these skills into your Immortal lineup can significantly bolster your overall strategy, providing a solid defense for your single Immortals and increasing your chances of emerging victorious in the dynamic world of Infinity Kingdom.

In conclusion, protecting your single immortals is a vital aspect of your Infinity Kingdom strategy. The skills like Fighting Master, Physical Shield, Life Link, and Void Realm offer valuable tools to shield your heroes from harm. Whether you’re safeguarding key frontline fighters or support immortals, these skills can make all the difference in the heat of battle. Fortify your single immortals, choose your skills wisely, and watch as they become unyielding champions in the world of Infinity Kingdom.

best-chase-trigger.title: Testing: Best Chase Trigger skill – Nova vs Death Breath vs Spell Disintegration
best-chase-trigger.description: Chase Triggering Skills – Comparing Nova, Death Breath, and Spell Disintegration
best-chase-trigger.html:
Chase Triggering Skills – Comparing Nova, Death Breath, and Spell Disintegration

This guide covers both the damage and Chase trigger potential of Toxin Nova, Death Breath, and Spell Disintegration.

It’s meant for players building crit-based Chase mages (like Empress Wu) who are trying to decide which single trigger skill to use — especially since we’re forced into Fighting Master until Fu Fei is maxed for crowd control immunity.

⚡ Chase

Chase deals 225% damage rate to all enemies when triggered and has a 30% chance to trigger on every magical critical hit made by the immortal that has Chase equipped.

So, what we’re looking for are skills that cause many frequent magical hits that can crit, since every magical crit gives us a roll to trigger Chase. More magical crits = more Chase activations.

Skill Breakdown and DPS Analysis

All damage calculations below assume there are 4 living enemies (to reflect Death Breath’s full AoE value).

Toxin Nova (or Fire Nova)

For Fire builds, you should always use Toxin Nova, not Fire Nova, since Fire Dragon’s Burn already occupies the burn debuff slot and cannot stack. (For other elements, they’re identical in output.)

  • Trigger Chance: 50% every 6 seconds.
  • Effect: 175% magical damage to 3 random enemies + DoT for 6 seconds (75% every 3 seconds, 2 ticks total).
  • Damage per trigger: (175 + 75 + 75) × 3 = 975% total damage per trigger.
  • DPS per trigger: 975 ÷ 6 = 162.5% DPS.
  • Effective DPS (50% proc chance): 81.25% DPS.

Death Breath

For Death Breath, we have a 100% trigger chance every 6 seconds, hitting all 4 enemies for 75% magical + 75% physical damage.

Damage per trigger (magical only): 75 × 4 = 300% magical damage per trigger.
DPS per trigger: 300 ÷ 6 = 50% DPS.
Final Effective DPS: 50%.

Note: In addition to this, Death Breath also deals 4 instances of 75% physical damage, which we’re not including in this calculation since we’re focusing on magical damage dealers (who have very low physical stats). You’ll still see slightly higher total damage than the 50% figure — particularly in early-game or low-stat environments where physical damage scales better.

Spell Disintegration

  • Trigger Chance: 50% every 3 seconds.
  • Effect: 125% magical damage to 3 enemies.
  • Damage per trigger: 125 × 3 = 375% total damage per trigger.
  • DPS per trigger: 375 ÷ 3 = 125% DPS.
  • Effective DPS (50% proc rate): 62.5%.

Quick Summary (4 Targets)

So, in terms of average DPS output, Nova remains highest, followed by Spell Disintegration, with Death Breath being the lowest — but the most consistent (since it always triggers).

⚔️ Chase Triggering Comparison

Chase triggers on magical critical hits, not just magical hits. Each magical crit gives one 30% chance to activate Chase.
So we care about how many magical damage instances each skill creates over time, and how consistent those hits are.

12-Second Window

  • Death Breath: 100% trigger chance, activates twice (6s and 12s), hitting 4 magical instances each time = 8 total magical hits.
  • Toxin Nova: 50% chance to trigger at 6s and 12s. Each activation hits 3 times instantly, plus 3 DoT ticks at 9s and 3 more at 12s if triggered. Average ~6 total hits.
  • Spell Disintegration: 50% chance every 3s, for 4 triggers in 12s, 3 hits each = 12 max, 6 average.

Result: Death Breath provides the most consistent total hits (8 guaranteed). Nova and Spell Disintegration have similar averages but depend on RNG.

15-Second Window

  • Death Breath: 8 total magical hits (4 hits × 2 triggers).
  • Toxin Nova: 50% chance × (3 instant + 6 DoT) = ~7.5 average hits.
  • Spell Disintegration: ~7.5 average hits.

They’re very close, but Death Breath maintains guaranteed uptime every 6s.

33-Second Example (4 Targets Alive)

In theory (assuming all 4 enemies remain alive), Nova averages 21 magical hits per fight, Death Breath guarantees 20, and Spell Disintegration averages around 15.
In reality, because enemies die at different times, Death Breath often loses total effective hits as the fight goes on, while Nova and Spell Disintegration continue hitting full value longer.

🧪 Testing Results – Nova vs Death Breath

Now let us move beyond the theoretical combat and try some testing. I played my fire march main to see which skill in reality gets more hits.

Nova produced roughly 40% more magical hits than Death Breath overall. This happens because DB’s AoE loses targets as enemies die, while Nova still hits its full 3.

🧪 Testing Results – Nova vs Spell Disintegration

Now let us test Spell Disintegration against the Nova which scored the best as purely trigger skill.

Nova still leads with about 20% more magical hits per fight, but the difference is not huge.
Spell Disintegration averaged 10.6 magical hits per fight, compared to Death Breath’s 10.1 in the first test — very close.

🧩 Interpretation

The above shows that Spell Disintegration is actually a slightly better trigger skill than Death Breath on average, though DB wins in early fight consistency.

In real fights, the first seconds are the most important, and we can safely assume that Death Breath will land more hits than Spell Disintegration early on, before one enemy immortal dies. Once an enemy falls, Spell Disintegration tends to catch up and then overtake DB in total magical hits as the fight continues.

Spell Disintegration also provides a strong magical defense debuff, increasing the effectiveness of your team’s overall damage — especially for ultimates and Chase hits.

So while Nova remains the best overall trigger, Spell Disintegration deserves real respect — it’s both efficient and supportive, and not far behind Nova in raw hit frequency.

⚖️ Which Should You Use?

If you’re running high crit (90%+):
→ Run Toxin Nova.
You’ll get the most Chase procs possible since nearly every magical hit crits, and Nova produces the most total damage instances overall. But you are exposed to RNG.

If you’re running mid crit (50–60% range):
→ Run Spell Disintegration.
You’ll get consistent trigger opportunities and the magic defense debuff, which helps your ultimates hit harder. If you are building around your ultimate ability being the absolute most important factor, you should do Spell Disintegration – although, in that case a concentration build is better for you than a chase one.
For example, a Water Chase build would prefer Spell Disintegration, since it doesn’t have the high crit rates of Fire builds.

If you’re running Death Breath:
→ Remember that while it’s not the best trigger in the long run, its 100% reliability is a huge advantage. If you dislike RNG, Death Breath is your friend.
Also, the more fragile (squishy) your build is, the more valuable DB and Spell Disintegration become — DB for reliability, and Spell Disintegration for its fast potential triggers at 3 seconds.

If your team can sustain longer and extend the “deciding” part of the fight beyond the first 12–20 seconds, then Nova becomes stronger as a trigger because it benefits from time smoothing out its RNG and can accumulate higher total activations (despite its slower 6-second cycle compared to Spell Disintegration’s 3s).

🧠 Final Thoughts

  • Nova = Best overall trigger; more total magical hits and higher DPS, but RNG-based and slower cycling (6s).
  • Spell Disintegration = Great balance; very close in hits to Nova, faster cycling (3s), and brings a valuable debuff.
  • Death Breath = Most consistent; 100% uptime, no RNG, and extra physical side damage early game.

If you want reliability and early pressure, go with Death Breath.
If you want balanced utility and sustained power, use Spell Disintegration.
If you want maximum burst potential and have the crit rate to back it up, Toxin Nova is still the #1 pick.

All three are viable — the choice depends on your crit rate, team durability, and comfort with RNG.

If you want to go deeper into the combat math or see full testing logs, feel free to tag me in the official IK Discord — always happy to go through the data. 😊

anger-vs-duel-master.title: Duel Master
anger-vs-duel-master.description: Player Guide: Mastering the “Duel Master” Skill in Infinity Kingdom
anger-vs-duel-master.html:
Player Guide: Mastering the “Duel Master” Skill in Infinity Kingdom

“Duel Master” is a skill in Infinity Kingdom that, while sometimes overlooked, holds considerable potential to elevate the effectiveness of physical damage dealers under the right conditions. Its dual functionality—boosting physical attack attributes and providing immunity to wound effects—makes it a versatile addition to any player’s arsenal, especially in strategies centered around sustained damage and healing.

Understanding “Duel Master”

Key Features

  • Physical Attack Increase: “Duel Master” boosts the physical attack attributes of the immortal by 50%. This increase, while not directly enhancing damage dealt, significantly strengthens the output of any physical damage dealer.

  • Immunity to Wound Effects: Perhaps the most distinguishing feature of “Duel Master” is its provision of immunity to wounds.

Wounds, a debuff applied by formidable immortals like Genghis Khan and Emperor Qin, prevent affected units from receiving healing (excluding shield effects). “Duel Master” counters this by making the equipped immortal immune to such effects, ensuring that healing abilities remain effective.

Strategic Applications

Optimizing Physical Damage Dealers

Given its attribute boost, “Duel Master” is naturally suited for immortals with a high physical damage output. The skill significantly enhances their combat effectiveness, making it a worthy consideration for any physical damage-focused strategy.

Countering Wound Effects

The immunity to wound effects provided by “Duel Master” is its standout feature, offering a critical counterplay to some of the game’s most potent debuffs. This aspect of the skill is invaluable in matchups where healing plays a pivotal role in maintaining frontline durability and overall team sustainability.

Ideal Immortal Pairings

  • Alexander in Earth or Hybrid Setups: Alexander benefits immensely from “Duel Master,” as his high attack speed and reliance on continuous healing make him a formidable force when paired with healers like Zenobia.
  • Other Physical Damage Dealers: While particularly impactful with Alexander, “Duel Master” can also enhance the effectiveness of other immortals such as Manco, Khubilai, or Gilgamesh, especially within holy setups, though its impact may vary.

Acquiring “Duel Master”

“Duel Master” distinguishes itself by being accessible and free to play, requiring only a low level for acquisition. This ease of access ensures that players at various stages of the game can leverage the skill’s benefits, from early exploration to late-game conquest strategies.

Conclusion

“Duel Master” offers a compelling mix of offensive enhancement and defensive resilience, making it a skill worthy of consideration for any player looking to optimize their physical damage dealers. Its ability to counteract one of the most debilitating debuffs in the game, coupled with a significant increase in physical attack attributes, provides a strategic edge in both PvP and PvE content. Whether you’re crafting a lineup around sustained healing and damage or looking for ways to enhance your existing physical attackers, “Duel Master” presents a robust solution that can adapt to various combat scenarios, solidifying its place in the end-game meta.

event-ranking-rewards.description: The Titantula Spider event is amazing if you know how to take full advantage. By building a solid team and consistently tanking in this event, you can boost your power significantly and save / supplement your spending a lot.
event-ranking-rewards.html:
The Titantula Spider event is amazing if you know how to take full advantage. By building a solid team and consistently tanking in this event, you can boost your power significantly and save / supplement your spending a lot.

The event occur twice a week on wednesday and sunday at fixed times. So setup your team, set the alarm on your phone and reap awesome rewards! This articles goes over the ranking part of the spider event, if you need info on the basic participation rewards, you can find them here.

Rewards

You should always try and get the last hit. Beware, that you must remain top 10 for the kill, but once that is secured, you should try and hit the killing blow. Be slow with it, it is better to miss your hit because someone else got the kill than to use an attack on a spider where you would have ranked top 10 anyway. The attack is refunded if you hit after the spider is dead.

Only exception to this, is if you are in close competition with someone and can see you will likely end on the same number of ranking points (event ranking). Then you want to hit quickly and get the point cap you both will reach – you want to do this, because if two players are tied in points, the player who got the points first wins.

Read my guides for info on how to setup your march right so you consistenly compete for the no. 1 ranking, e.g. my guide for killing blow tips n tricks.

Rewards from attacks on spider are as follow.

Tips n tricks

Getting killing blows require some finess and a good bit of luck.

You need to make yourself a march that deals around 1% in damage, reliably. See my guides on marches.

When the spider is active, you need to watch carefully who in your server turns up, watch the damage meter and how much power the attendees have. Based on this you can aproximate their damage dealt per hit and count down to the killing blow.

I usually use the last 30% to take note of the attacks. I move quickly from each of the three spider spawns and simply count attacks landing on the spider (take note if high power people are idle untill last min you wanna adjust accordingly). When the spider have droppedn from 30% to 20% I note how many attacks were made – e.g. let’s say 15. If from 20% to 10% takes 13 hits, I will then make sure that my last attack is made as the 13th attack move towards the spider.

If powerful people are at spider trying to snipe it, I will subtract a chunck of hits and go when I have seen 10 armies marching.

dragon.description: Once your castle has reached Level 5 the Dragon Cave will become unlocked, and you will be able to enter it to hatch and raise dragons in order to add a fifth member to your party when you prepare for battle.
dragon.html:
Once your castle has reached Level 5 the Dragon Cave will become unlocked, and you will be able to enter it to hatch and raise dragons in order to add a fifth member to your party when you prepare for battle.

There are five different types of dragons in Infinity Kingdom and each one is tied to an element – Water, Water, Earth, Wind, and Lightning. Each of these dragons has 5 maturity stages – Egg, Infancy, Adolescence, Adulthood, and Elder.

Dragon Upgrades

You will need dragon soul crystals in order to hatch a dragon egg when you reach Level 5 and unlock the Dragon Cave. Dragon soul crystals can be acquired as rewards from world bosses, quests and events. Once the dragon egg has hatched, you will be able to raise and upgrade your dragon by spending gold, which can be obtained from the Coin Mint and Dwellings buildings. You will be able to train a dragon when you see a dragon icon bubble above the Dragon Cave. When your dragon reaches level 5, 15, and 25 you will unlock skills for them. This skill and their effects can be upgraded by spending Dragon Soul Crystals.

Read all about how to obtain dragon crystals here!

shops.description: Whether you’re a light spender or a whale, knowing where to spend your resources is key to efficient progression in Infinity Kingdom. shops.html:
🛒 Infinity Kingdom In-Game Shops Guide: What to Buy

Whether you’re a light spender or a whale, knowing where to spend your resources is key to efficient progression in Infinity Kingdom. This guide walks through all the day-to-day in-game shops and outlines what’s worth your investment — and what isn’t. We are not going to cover all the standard bundles, since most of them are too expensive to consistently buy for normal players and you should buy from there only if you really need something. We are going to cover the in-game shops which are either free or very cheap and efficient. 

⚔️ Arena Shop

The Arena Shop can be deceptive. While it offers a variety of items, almost all of them are bad value compared to other sources. The two standout exceptions are Stardust, which is always in demand for portait levels, and the big 2400 Wind Dragon Crystals, which are priced far more rare than other dragon shards. Even if you’re not building Wind, it’s wise to collect these for potential future use or to save resources if you ever need Wind (especially with the new buff in patch 2.8.2). Small dragon crystal bundles here are a massive trap — they look tempting but offer extremely poor shard-per-cost ratios.

✅ Buy:

  • Stardust – A must-buy every time it appears.
  • Big Gold Bundle Wind Dragon Crystals – Even if you’re not building Wind, these are great value.

❌ Avoid:

  • Other dragon crystals – Horribly overpriced. For example, 40,000 arena coins may give you 800 shards vs. 6,000 in the Wind pack — over 7x less value.

🧭 Mysterium Shop

This shop rotates based on Mysterium progress and offers one of the few ways to get Elite Artifacts (EAs) without relying on luck or cash. If you’re developing an Immortal that’s missing their artifact, this should be your top priority.

✅ Buy:

  • Elite Artifacts (EAs) for Immortals you actively use.
  • Only consider other items after you’re done with EAs.

❌ Avoid:

  • Teleports on Main – Use alt-account inventories for porting instead and CoR shop.

🔄 Triss Shop (Skill Recycle Shop)

This shop is critical for developing a strong march. It lets you recycle unwanted skills into a unique currency to buy top-tier ones. Since meta skills like No Escape, Purify, Weakening Curse, define competitive play, you should always prioritize these. Artifacts are a secondary option once your core builds are complete. Avoid using this shop to grab UAs unless in very niche cases like if you cannot obtain e.g. Trajan’s elsewhere — they are often freely available from events and not worth the spend here.

✅ Buy:

  • Top-tier Skills only (e.g. No Escape, Energy Burst, etc.).
  • Artifacts only if you’re done with key skills.

❌ Avoid:

  • Low-tier skills – They offer no real advantage and waste your currency.

🛡️ Alliance Shop

Simple and essential: Space Portals are the only purchase that makes sense in this shop. These normally cost real money, but here you get them free just for contributing to alliance tech or donating during KVK. Even if you don’t currently need to teleport, having a stockpile means you’re ready for war, server merges, or emergency jumps. No other items in the shop come close in value.

✅ Buy:

  • Space Portals – Normally $5 each, totally free here with steady coin flow.

❌ Avoid:

  • Everything else – Cost per value is significantly worse than the portals.

🌟 Golden Path Merit Shop

This shop is a jackpot for mid-to-late-game players. You earn merit through Golden Path missions and can use it for powerful Immortals, AP, dragons, Stardust, and even portals. Dragon Castle Skins like Mountain can offer great utility, while Immortals like YSS are excellent long-term investments. The shop is very flexible, making it great for plugging resource gaps. You can even buy Stardust here in a pinch. Frames and chat skins are purely aesthetic but available for collectors.

✅ Buy:

  • Important Dragons – Based on your team comp (Mountain is great early).
  • Core Immortals – YSS, Trajan, etc.
  • Big AP Pots – Excellent value for long-term farming or raids.
  • Space Portals – Backup if you’re short elsewhere. Personally I like to obtain them here too as long as I am below my threshold. When I hit my count I collect only from Alliance shop etc.

Optional:

  • Stardust – Rare and useful but expensive pick here.
  • Frames & Chat Skins – If you care about cosmetics.

❌ Avoid:

  • Artifacts here – Usually more efficient to get elsewhere (Mysterium, Triss).

💠 Pearl Shop (Daily Purchase)

This is one of the game’s most flexible shops for spenders. You earn Pearls from spending and can convert them into valuable resources. Sun and Power Crystals are your best value here for building equipment. You can also grab Dust, which is rare and needed in large amounts. Occasionally, you can use Pearls to finish key Immortals (like grabbing a few shards for Alex to unlock his specialization). Avoid buying keys or Shadow Crystals unless you’re spending heavily or chasing something specific. Personally I like to stack Pearls to buy Epic Dragon Chest Keys, but only while you are in dire need of crystals as you rapidly progress in e.g. season 1 and 2.

✅ Buy:

  • Sun & Power Crystals – Excellent cost efficiency for equipment growth.
  • Dust – Needed for specializations; hard to farm.

Optional:

  • Immortals – Finish specific units if close.
  • Keys – Only in progress stage.

❌ Avoid:

  • Shadow Crystals – Overpriced for their value.

💎 VIP Shop

Reserved for long-term or heavy spenders, this shop lets you spend VIP Points on premium items. Most notably, it’s where you can unlock Holy and Shadow Dragons, but you’ll need to focus on one. Splitting between both is too expensive. Unless you’re a super whale, pick one and commit. Everything else in the shop is filler — some players grab epic chests during dragon rushes, but most regret it later. If you’re under VIP 15, you may want to push VIP using gems slowly over time — it’s a long but worthwhile goal!

✅ Buy:

  • Holy or Shadow Dragon – Best investment of your VIP points.
    • Holy Dragon is top-tier, great synergy and power.
    • Shadow Dragon has unique combos — niche but strong.

❌ Avoid:

  • Epic chests, gear, etc. – Poor long-term value.
  • Trying to get both dragons – Focus on one or you’ll stagnate.

🪙 VIP with Gems?

If you’re not VIP 15 yet:

  • Spending gems to reach VIP 15 over time is viable.
  • Especially good in big alliances where you get lots of free VIP points.

🏪 Standard Gem Shop

The “default” gem shop looks like a place to grab quick resources — but in practice, it’s just a price anchor. Almost everything here is full price and rarely worth it. Treat it as a reference point to know what’s overpriced, and only buy here in one situation: using gems to push VIP level when nearing milestones like VIP 15.

❌ Avoid:

  • Everything — It’s full price. You’ll find better deals almost anywhere else.

✅ Only exception:

  • VIP Points – If you’re gem-pushing to hit VIP milestones.

seven-day-bundle.html:
With Patch 2.8.2, Infinity Kingdom introduced a brand-new seven-day bundle system, a recurring micro-spending feature aimed at giving players daily rewards for a limited time. The idea is simple: purchase a low-cost bundle for seven consecutive days, and if you buy five of them, you unlock a bonus chest.

On paper, this sounds like an appealing, low-commitment way to stack up on rare resources — but is it actually worth it?

Let’s break it down.

🔍 How the Seven-Day Bundle Works

The bundles come in daily rotation. Each day, for seven days, you have the option to purchase a bundle box, usually priced between $2–3 USD. If you purchase at least five out of the seven, you unlock a bonus chest at the end of the cycle.

The contents of the bundles vary by rotation and even by server season (e.g. early game vs. Conquest), and so far we’ve seen:

🧪 First Rotation – Philosopher Stones

  • Cost: $2/day
  • Contents:
    • 3x Philosopher Stones
    • 60x Saladin Fragments (bonus unlock across the week)
    • Bonus Chest: Full Saladin unlock + additional resources

This was arguably one of the better-value bundles, especially for newer players. You’re essentially getting 15 Philosopher Stones and a legendary Immortal for around $10, plus some gems and extras. Not game-breaking, but decent value — especially if you’re low on purple crystals for shop rotations.

Still, for spenders who already participate in seasonal bundles and events like Golden Path, purple crystals will come by the hundreds just from melting fragments. So this bundle, while reasonable, won’t be essential for most.

🔧 Second Rotation – Artifact Fragments

  • Cost: $3/day
  • Contents:
    • 5x Random Artifact Fragments per day
    • Bonus Chest: A non-unique full artifact
    • Some materials and gems

Unfortunately, this bundle is not recommended. Regular artifacts (i.e., not unique or legendary ones) are simply not valuable, even in early seasons like Season 1. By the time you’re chasing artifacts, you’re usually in a position where skill stones or energy-based skills are a much better investment. Spending $15 for normal artifact fragments is hard to justify.

🔥 Conquest Rotation – Dragon Talents (Dragon Essences)

  • Cost: $3/day
  • Contents:
    • Dragon Talent Stones (Essences)
    • Bonus: Additional essences or resources

This one is situationally valuable. In early Conquest, when you’re just starting to develop Dragon Talents, essences can be a limiting factor. The bundle offers a manageable way to speed up that progression. That said, over time, most active Conquest players will accumulate more than enough essences through regular gameplay — so it’s a good early boost, but not a long-term value.

💸 Verdict – Should You Buy?

Let’s be blunt — most of these bundles are not worth your money.

The $2 Philosopher Stone bundle is decent for early-game spenders who need cheap purple crystals or want a quick Immortal unlock. Even then, it’s mostly convenience, not necessity.

The $3 artifact fragment bundle is, frankly, terrible value. You’re better off saving for better bundles or spending that money on Tower of Knowledge skill shards, event packs, or VIP upgrades.

The Dragon Essence bundle for Conquest players is situationally useful, but only if you’re in the early stages of developing your Dragon Talents. Later, you’ll have more than you can spend.

🔑 Summary

  • ✅ Philosopher Stones Bundle ($2): Okay value, especially for unlocking a specific Immortal like Saladin. Decent if you’re short on purple crystals.
  • ❌ Artifact Fragment Bundle ($3): Not recommended. Regular artifacts are cheap, common, and mostly irrelevant.
  • ⚖️ Dragon Essence Bundle ($3): Good early Conquest boost, but falls off in value quickly.

Ultimately, if you’re a spender, you’re probably better off putting your money into event packs with high-end skill shards, ToK unlocks, or VIP progress. These bundles aren’t predatory, but they’re not game-changers either.
