Don’t miss out on free gems, Philosopher’s Stones, speedups, and the cozy Moonlit Hearth castle skin for just 100 points — basically free!
golden-week.html:
✨ Golden Week is here in Infinity Kingdom! ✨
Make sure you log in through the Gtarcade App and collect your free rewards before November 7th. Don’t miss out on free gems, Philosopher’s Stones, speedups, and the cozy Moonlit Hearth castle skin for just 100 points — basically free!

Golden Week is here in Norheim, and Gtarcade is giving us some small but sweet rewards through the App (desktop or mobile). Until November 7th, players can grab both a free bundle and a super cheap skin reward. Neither is game-breaking, but for free-to-play players and collectors, this is an easy win.

Free Golden Week Giftpack

The free pack is the one nobody should skip. This is a daily reward, so make sure you login to the Gtarcade app every day atleast for the Golden Week!

It gives you:

  • 300 Gems
  • 9 Philosopher’s Stones
  • 3 Hours of Universal Speedups
  • A small stack of resources

The real gem here (no pun intended) is the Philosopher’s Stones, since you can convert them into Soul Crystals or use them for Immortal summons. Every player benefits from these — F2P especially, but even late-game players can’t say no to free pulls.

So yeah, this is basically just free efficiency. Claim it the moment you log in on the Gtarcade app.

Moonlit Hearth Castle Skin (100 Gtarcade Points)

Now, onto the second Golden Week gift: the Moonlit Hearth castle skin. This one is not a paid cash bundle — it costs just 100 Gtarcade Points, which makes it dirt cheap.

To put it in perspective:

  • Just doing your daily login and spinning the Gtarcade Point Wheel once basically gets you there.
  • Even if you don’t have points saved up, you’ll almost certainly collect enough during the Golden Week period to buy it without effort.

That’s why I’d actually call this practically free-to-play, even though technically you’re spending points.

The skin itself is a cozy purple design with an Asian aesthetic. Not flashy, not over the top — just a chill vibe. It comes with:

  • +3% Resource Gathering Speed buff

And let’s be honest: that buff isn’t great. Gathering speed doesn’t impact combat, and compared to skins with training, healing, or construction boosts, this one sits low on the usefulness scale.

But here’s the thing: at 100 points, the opportunity cost is tiny. Sure, you could spend those points on:

  • Two daily Beginner Gtarcade bundles (15-min speedups + 1 small SP bottle each), or
  • Roughly a third of the 100-gem bundle

But for most players, that tradeoff is worth it just to snag a limited-time cosmetic. If you like the cozy look, it’s a no-brainer.

You should expect to earn over 100 point for free just by doing the daily Gtarcade routine in the App, making the cost very very minor. Read more about the ways to obtain Points for free here.

Player Perspective, i.e. what I will do:

  • Grab the free bundle immediately (Philosopher’s Stones are always high value).
  • Spend the 100 points on the Moonlit Hearth skin — not because the buff is good, but because it’s so cheap and it adds to my collection of skins. Its cute and passing it up seems a wasted opportunity given the incredibly low cost.

What if my Account is not bound to a Gtarcade account?

First of all, I recommend that you fix that immediately. Simply the risk of account deletion, forgetting the password, loosing your phone, etc. is more than enough risk to make Gtarcade Account Binding an important step for you. If this is relevant for you, read more here.

How to acces the Gtarcade App?

Using the Desktop app you find the giftpacks under “Point Shop” as you open the Gtarcade app as you would normally when starting the game. If you do not have the app, download available here.

On Mobile, you can download the App via your preferred App Store or access directly using the in-game shop which has a link at the top. See more below.

Now if you are wondering why the two Golden Week bundles are not in my video here, its just because I redeemed them via Desktop. They will be in yours.

That’s it! Happy Golden Week – go get those free rewards!

ruins.title: Super-Ruins (level 4): Rewards Bonus After Scouting all Ruins in Norheim
ruins.description: Super-Ruins Guide – The Ultimate Ruin Event
ruins.html:
Super-Ruins Guide – The Ultimate Ruin Event

Ruins are scattered locations on the map in Infinity Kingdom that can be scouted for valuable rewards. These ruins come in three levels (1-3), with higher levels offering better rewards. To find them, you must send your scout to search different areas of the map. Once scouted, they will yield a variety of useful items including gems, action points, VIP points, and more.

How to Scout Ruins Efficiently

  1. Use your scout to search for ruins across the map.
  2. Ruins are found in multiple zones, so you must check every area to fully complete the scouting event.
  3. Each ruin has a level (1, 2, or 3), with level 3 offering the best rewards.
  4. Keep an eye on the progress bar—it tracks how many ruins you’ve scouted.
  5. Once you have scouted every single ruin on the map, you will unlock the powerful Super-Ruins.

What Are Super-Ruins?

Super-Ruins are special ruins that appear only after you complete the normal Ruin event. Once you’ve scouted every ruin and filled the progress bar, these ruins will begin appearing on your map. They are marked in purple and provide even greater rewards than Level 3 ruins.

How Often Do Super-Ruins Appear?

  • Super-Ruins will spawn continuously throughout the day. You can have a total of 5 at a time through the Clues mechanic. Make sure to ALWAYS scout these and keep the Clues cooldown working for you.
  • These ruins keep coming back, meaning you can continue farming them for extended rewards. There are no cap on these and they will continue to spawn for eternity!

Why Are Super-Ruins So Valuable?

Unlike normal ruins, Super-Ruins offer even better rewards because they include a Level 4 tier. This makes them the best ruins in the game for farming high-value items.

Rewards from Super-Ruins

Super-Ruins have a random chance to drop rewards, but because they include Level 3 and Level 4 tiers, your chances of getting top-tier loot are much better. Some of the best rewards include:

  • Gems 💎
  • Contract Builders 🏗️ (essential for fast progress!)
  • Action Points (AP) ⚡
  • Purple Crystals 🔮
  • Philosopher’s Stones 🧙 (for immortals!)
  • VIP Points 🎖️

Conclusion: Always Scout for Super-Ruins!

If you haven’t finished scouting all the normal ruins yet, do it as soon as possible to unlock Super-Ruins. The benefits are enormous, and they provide a consistent way to gain huge amounts of resources every day. Stay active, check your map frequently, and farm as many Super-Ruins as you can!

Happy Scouting! 🚀

patch-notes.description: Time Rift Breaker – A Game-Changing Event
patch-notes.html:
Time Rift Breaker – A Game-Changing Event

The Time Rift Breaker event is unquestionably one of the most anticipated additions in Version 2.6.2. It promises to be a game-changer, reminiscent of the beloved Spider event, but on a grander scale. This cross-server event invites lords from the same season to unite and confront a formidable adversary. It introduces a dynamic twist to the gameplay, where lords must strategize based on elemental weaknesses, adding an extra layer of depth to battles. With different elemental weaknesses and a prolonged cross-server format, it’s an event that holds immense promise and anticipation.

Time Rift Breaker 101 – A Cross-Server Challenge

One of the standout additions to Infinity Kingdom in Version 2.6.2 is the Time Rift Breaker event. This is a cross-server event that allows lords from the same season to come together and challenge a formidable adversary. To access the event, simply tap on the “Well of Time” located in the bottom-right corner of your screen.

Event Requirements:

  • Your server must have entered Season 2.
  • Your Castle Level must be equal to or higher than Level 15.

Event Period:

  • The event starts every Monday at 00:00 (UTC) and concludes every Sunday at 24:00 (UTC).
  • During the first two days (Monday to Wednesday), the enemy is in the recharge and incubation stage and cannot be attacked.
  • The challenge stage begins every Thursday at 00:00 (UTC) and runs until Sunday at 24:00 (UTC). During this period, you can attack the enemy. If defeated, the enemy will resurrect after a certain time or escape if not defeated.

Event Rules:

  • Each lord has three challenge attempts daily.
  • All battles in this event are automatic.
  • Immortals deployed in a challenge cannot be used again on the same day.
  • Utilize Immortals of the corresponding elements to deal additional damage based on the Time Rift Breaker’s elemental weakness.

Event Rewards:

  • The event offers a variety of rewards, including Total Damage Ranking Rewards, Highest Damage Ranking Rewards, Kill Rewards, and Honor Rewards.
  • These rewards will grant you Space-Time Glory Badges, which can be exchanged for valuable items in the shop.

A brand new awesome event

The Time Rift Breaker event stands out as a cross-server extravaganza, allowing lords from the same season to unite in a shared challenge. This feature brings a sense of unity and camaraderie among players who might have previously been isolated within their servers. The prospect of joining forces with lords from other realms introduces an exciting new dimension to the game, fostering a sense of community beyond one’s server.

What sets this event apart is its elemental complexity. Lords must carefully strategize, considering the elemental strengths and weaknesses of their Immortals. This strategic layer adds depth to battles, making every choice and move count. It’s a feature that rewards thoughtful planning and diversity in Immortal selection, ultimately leading to more engaging and dynamic encounters.

Cross-Server Unity: The Time Rift Breaker is not just a server-specific event. It’s a cross-server extravaganza that brings lords from different seasons together. This unification breaks down barriers and fosters a sense of community beyond individual servers. Players will forge new alliances, share knowledge, and face challenges together. It’s a step towards a more connected and immersive gaming experience.

Extended Engagement: The event’s format, spanning from Monday to Sunday each week, ensures that lords have ample time to participate and immerse themselves in the action. The inclusion of incubation and challenge stages adds a unique rhythm to the event, keeping players eagerly anticipating each stage’s trials.

Strategy Meets Rewards: With each lord granted three daily challenge attempts, strategy becomes paramount. Every move must be calculated to maximize success. The rewards on offer, including Total Damage Ranking Rewards, Highest Damage Ranking Rewards, Kill Rewards, and Honor Rewards, provide compelling incentives for participation. Space-Time Glory Badges, the event’s currency, can be exchanged for valuable items in the shop, further fueling the competitive spirit.

In summary, the Time Rift Breaker is an event that’s generating immense anticipation. It promises to be the hallmark of Infinity Kingdom’s gaming experience, offering a blend of excitement, strategy, and camaraderie that players eagerly await. With its promise of being an enhanced version of the beloved Spider event, different elemental dynamics, and an expansive cross-server format, the Time Rift Breaker is poised to be a game-changer that players can’t wait to dive into. It’s an event that holds the potential to reshape the very fabric of the Infinity Kingdom.

patch-2-8-9.title: Himiko Earth meta build – Vader’s setup from patch 2.8.9
patch-2-8-9.description: King Vader’s Himiko Earth Meta Build — A Veteran Analysis on his top tier meta build
patch-2-8-9.html:
King Vader’s Himiko Earth Meta Build — A Veteran Analysis on his top tier meta build

Introduction

Across multiple seasons, Earth–Himiko has settled into one of the most reliable endgame archetypes in Infinity Kingdom. What separates average versions from top-tier variants, however, is the discipline to allocate spending and skillstones efficiently while understanding the mechanics that make the composition resilient.

King Vader’s (s344) build represents the “finished” form of this lineup: a configuration polished through testing against mirror Earth teams, high-spender Shadow variants, and even Fu Fei–anchored control cores. After speaking with him at length, the strengths of his approach became clear. It is a measured, sustain-oriented Earth base whose entire structure exists to give Himiko the sustain she needs to carry the victory home, clean windows to crit, and maximum troop preservation.

Below is a detailed breakdown of his setup and why it consistently outperforms even into difficult matchups. Before going over the details, you can also watch this short video to see more details on performance and how Vader is able to beat whales at a disadvantage both in terms of Legendary Immortals, Legendary Skills and simple raw STP. Enjoy!

Immortal Lineup

Theodora — Sustain Engine and DOT Cleanser

Theodora remains the most practical choice for players not committed to the extreme expenditure required to finish a Fu Fei talent tree. While Fu Fei technically edges her out at absolute peak investment, Vader’s results reinforce a simple truth: most players get far more value directing money into skillstones and artifacts instead of forcing Fu Fei early.

Her value in this lineup comes from:

  • Frequent, stable healing that complements the long fight durations the of Earth cores that assist her in sustaining this team so well.
  • DOT removal, which is crucial in matchups against Shadow (Blade Vortex), lightning compositions, and any setup built around stacking DoT effects (damage over time).

Artifact:
A Surge artifact for increased regeneration rate. This improves both healing consistency and given increased regen rate you will clear DoT effects more consistently as well as trigger Spring of Life more frequently as surge is allowing her to cycle heals faster.

Talent:

  • Battle Excitation — mandatory for initial energy on our Himiko as well as for the damage amp it contributes to Himiko, overall a significant tempo gain.

Himiko — Primary Damage and Backline Control

Himiko is the centerpiece. Beyond her raw damage, her targeting logic—always landing her control on the enemy backliner with the highest HP—allows her to directly pressure sustain teams and punish compositions relying on a single protected carry if they neglect to run Fighting Master.

What elevates her here is the synergy between:

  • Shadow elemental advantage (beating every element except Holy),
  • High crit scaling as a mage, and
  • Massive AoE pressure, avoiding any risk of not hitting your desired enemy target (compared to e.g. Empress Wu where you can get unlucky and not hit the enemy’s carry with multiple ultimates)

Artifact:

  • Crit% main stat
  • Annihilation bonus
    This combination is the highest-value damage profile available to her. For secondary attributes, if you can get more crit % that is a big advantage, that being said, crit value and magical damage is also very helpful.

Talent:

  • Stormeye — essential for amplifying her overall damage through raw damage modifier and its boost to crit chance.

Yi Sun-Shin (YSS) — Damage Reduction and Tempo Control

YSS performs two jobs exceptionally well in this team:

  1. He protects the team from collapse via his huge 30% damage taken reduction and provides a significant 30% healing buff while under his effect.
  2. He disrupts opposing Alex lines by simply being placed in front of them, because we are running Fearless Stance to reduce damage taken, turning him into a durable brick wall.

Artifact:

  • Physical Defense % as the top attribute
  • Growth as the bonus
    Growth gives value into both physical and magical matchups, making it the most efficient single artifact choice for the long term. If you are able to craft two artifacts maxed with physical defense % top, then you can have a Guard bonus artifact in your inventory and equip this when fighting into physical damage enemies – especially when using YSS to tank an enemy Alex or other high physical damage dealers.

This contribution is one reason the build holds up so well against other top builds. YSS provides invaluable mitigation effects and ensures the rest of our sustain setup has time to do its job.

Bjorn — Resilience Boons and Damage amp

Bjorn is an incredible choice for the second tank in this Earth–Himiko. He provides:

  • A debuff increasing the damage taken by the enemy by 20%
  • A resilience buff of 30% defending our frontlines against critical hits.
  • And his shadow affinity also gives him an advantage as he takes reduced damage from all other elements than holy.

Talent:

  • Sturdy Barrier, which supplies shields across the lineup—an important layer in a sustain-based structure and given the sustain focus and high mitigation of this setup, you will actually see very high shield-values from an upgraded Sturdy Barrier talent – unlike on many other more squishy setups where damage is taken too quickly for Study to have a real impact.

Artifact:

  • Physical Defense % with Growth bonus
    Against magic-heavy enemies, Growth outperforms Guard, and late-game players generally maintain both options for matchup flexibility. Vader currently has a Guard artifact, but a slight improvement would be to have a Growth one and change between the two as needed.

Skill Setup

Bjorn

  • Purification: Cleanses debuffs and triggers small heals, which in turn activate Spring of Life‘s 15% reduced damage taken buff.
  • Energy Shield: Core mitigation; prevents unnecessary troop loss across the board through powerful shield effects. Mitigation/sustain through shielding is superior to raw healing, simply because there is no loss of troop count. When you take damage from an enemy you loose troops, healing will revive these troops, but in the interim you are left with reduced troop counts. For example, a Himiko taking damage: If she has shields up to absorb the damage, she loses no troops at all. If she does not, she loses troops which reduces her damage until she is healed back up. So even at identical values, shielding is technically superior to healing.
  • Weakness Aura: Simple, cuts down on enemy resilience, reinforcing Himiko’s crit reliability.

Temporary options:
If you lack skillstones and are looking for alternatives as you progress into the skill setup above. I suggest using skills such as: Blessing of Rage, Blessing of Defense, or Oaken Guard.

Yi Sun-Shin

  • Energy Suppression: Reduces enemy energy gain, slowing down the energy regen of your enemies is a powerful method of mitigating damage.
  • Weakening Curse: Disarms physical damage dealers, extremely valuable versus physical damage dealers, e.g. Alexanders.
  • Master’s Aegis: Major magical mitigation; this is one of the core reasons why the build is so stable in a mage-heavy meta.
    • If you are fighting into a physical damage enemy or meta in general, then you should not run Master’s Aegis but instead opt for a Heart of Arcana for your aura slot here.

Budget alternative:
Run Oaken Guard or Resist in place of Weakening Curse / Aegis, until your Wisdom Well/Cinder skills are completed.

Theodora

  • Vitality Touch: Core source of healing and a reliable trigger for Spring of Life and a nice mitigation effect.
  • Spring of Life: Increases all healing effects and provides a strong mitigation buff once immortals are healed. Raises overall survivability and strengthens your heals.
  • Assist: Essential for preserving Himiko’s troop count, which directly affects her damage output. Absolutely mandatory in all builds that rely on a carry-backline damage dealer.

Temporary substitutes:
Rage Blessing, Blessing of Defense/Oaken Guard/Resist, and Malice Aura can fill gaps during early construction, depending on what you are fighting against.

Fighting into No Escape

Important notes for fighting into No Escape setups: If you are fighting into enemies that rely on No Escape, Fountain of Life becomes a must have legendary skill. Having it at level 1 is perfectly fine, but you need it to counter No Escape. That being said, on many servers and in many KvKs you will find that many are not using No Escape on their main march simply because of how common Fountain of Life has become. If you do face No Escape enemies, you need to equip Fountain of Life on Theodora, move Spring of Life to YSS in place of Energy Suppression which you move to Bjorn and give up Purification.

For this feature on Vader’s build, he is not fighting into No Escape builds often and hence do not use Fountain of Life by default. Note that upgrading fountain of life to higher levels will also provide enough healing output that you should baseline it into the setup. But as money is not infinite, keeping a level 1 on the sidelines to swap in while you prioritize other skills is a good strategy.

Himiko

  • Annihilation: While Infinite Firepower is best-in-slot for raw damage, short of being able to afford multiple high level legendary skills, Vader is using Annihilation until he completes Infinite Firepower.
  • Energy Master: Top-tier for both damage and energy cycling; expensive, but the improvement is immediate as this skill enables fast ultimate-cycling. Later can be paired with Corrosive Power when you are able to get it (amongst the most expensive skill in the game).
    • Spell Disintegration works well as a placeholder until Energy Master reaches level 5.
  • Fighting Master — mandatory unless you run Fu Fei. Control immunity is non-negotiable for your primary carry.

Dragon setup

Vader is running this build with the Earth Dragon Dementer and using the Collapse dragon specialization talent tree. The earth dragon provides unrivaled mitigation effects in its Sandstorm Breath and with Collapse we max out on the mitigation effect which works perfect in synergy with our core setup here. Collapse increases both the chance of the mitigation buff taking effect (to 98% from 90% base) and provides increased duration of the effect (16.8 seconds from 12 seconds base).

As an added advantage to simply being perfect for this build, the earth dragon is also a free-to-play dragon meaning you can upgrade its talents with Dragon Crystals from elemental bosses without having to spend on events like with the Shadow dragon.

Talking to Vader, his take is that if he did want to spend on a paywalled dragon (holy / shadow) he would opt for the holy dragon for its healing and mitigation effects. That being said, he does not think this would be a real benefit to the build as the mitigation from Dementer is simply amazing! And for the record, I personally agree with that statement.

Player Perspective — Why Vader’s Version Works

What impressed me most in testing variants of this structure is its remarkable matchup stability. Earth–Himiko traditionally wins long fights, but it often struggles to maintain troop advantage when pressured early by optimized Shadow or by other burst-heavy builds. Vader’s version seem to consistently be able to sustain and take advantage of superior troop counts.

In practice, this lets Himiko maintain effective DPS deep into the fight, even against enemy carries with higher level legendary skills and Fu Fei support. I am very impressed with the performance – and consistent performance – of Vader’s build here. Hence I am very happy that he has taken the time to talk it through so I can publish it here on the wiki for many others to read and learn from. Thank you King Vader for your contribution to the community!

Conclusion

Vader’s Himiko Earth build represents a very well engineered conquest setup. While progress is yet to be made towards the final endgame form of the composition (legendary progress for skills and Fu Fei eventually) this build is a prime example of a sustain- and mitigation-heavy shell enabling a crit-focused, high-pressure Himiko. What makes it extreemly interesting for me to see and share, is that Vader prooves it doesn’t demand early Fu Fei investment; instead, by channeling his spending into the skills and artifacts he is able to actually deliver matchup wins against others who on the face of it should have the advantage (check the video in the top if you have not yet).

For players building toward a long-term Earth-Himiko lineup, this is in my opinion the most reliable blueprint currently available as of time of writing. Huge thank you to King Vader of server 344 for sharing this awesome build with us all!

patch-2-8-8.title: Patch 2.8.8 – Legendary Season
patch-2-8-8.description: The Wildfire Furnace embers are burning hot and the team behind IK is ready to drop the new Legendary Season, introducing level 60 cap across buildings, Immortals, dragons, gnomes, tech—the works.  With new ranks, levels and tiers comes new materials and systems:
patch-2-8-8.html:
The Wildfire Furnace embers are burning hot and the team behind IK is ready to drop the new Legendary Season, introducing level 60 cap across buildings, Immortals, dragons, gnomes, tech—the works. With new ranks, levels and tiers comes new materials and systems:

  • Energy Core gating for building upgrades (new currencies: Azure & Stellar Crystals).
  • Mythic equipment reforges with random attributes (bound to the Immortal).
  • Elemental Domain boss dungeons on a weekly elemental schedule.
  • Alliance-based KVK registration and new migration rules centered on a server-wide Command Power metric.

This guide translates the patch notes into practical gameplay: what changes, why it matters, and how to prep so day one of Legendary Season feels like an acceleration, not a wall.

Full patch notes available here.

Level 60 Expansion – What Actually Changes

1) Buildings → 60 via Energy Cores

Energy Cores control your path to Lv60. Each Core has 5 tiers, every tier has 3 stages. You inject energy with Azure or Stellar Crystals; once a Core hits stage 3, you can upgrade to the next tier by consuming normal resources.

  • Azure Crystals: After entering Legendary Season and reaching Forge Lv55, you can convert Food/Wood/Stone/Iron into Azure in the Forge.
  • Stellar Crystals: From events (details vary per cycle).

Why this matters: You can’t brute-force to 60 with only speedups and mats. The Core stages throttle pace. Start thinking of resource → Azure conversion as a long-term sink, and time your event play for Stellar injections.

Prep tips

  • Push Forge to 55 before Oct 20 if you can, so Azure conversion is unlocked immediately once you’re in Legendary.
  • Bank standard resources and speedups; you’ll redirect a chunk into Azure instead of raw building.

2) Equipment → Legendary+ & Mythic Reforges

Gnomes Lv56+ can drop Legendary+ gear that levels to 60. Once strengthened to 60, you can reforge to Mythic using:

  • [Class + Slot Forging Stone] and [Forging Hammer] to perform the reforge.
  • Reforged Mythic pieces are bound to the Immortal, cannot be removed, and gain 1–5 random attributes.
  • Rerolls: Use Tempering Elixirs + Forging Hammers to reroll random attributes.
  • Sources for these mats: Well of Time – Elemental Domain (see below).

Why this matters: Mythic attributes are the real stat ceiling. Binding means fewer hand-me-downs; plan who gets Mythic first. The random lines introduce chase/variance like Artifacts—expect a min–max grind.

Prep tips

  • Farm and stash Well of Time currency; clear daily once Legendary starts.
  • Decide priority Immortals per march; once you bind a Mythic, it’s committed.
  • Keep a reroll budget (Elixirs/Hammers) to avoid getting stuck with dead stats.

3) Elemental Domain (Oct 20, 00:00 UTC)

A new event featuring eight elemental dungeons: Water, Fire, Wind, Lightning, Earth, Holy, Shadow, Chaos.

Weekly schedule

  • Mon: Water
  • Tue: Fire
  • Wed: Wind
  • Thu: Lightning
  • Fri: Earth
  • Sat–Sun: All elements (Water, Fire, Wind, Lightning, Earth, Holy, Shadow, Chaos)

Rules

  • Element lock: Only Immortals/dragons of that element can enter that day’s dungeon.
  • 3 challenges/day; attempts reset daily.
  • Rewards scale with boss remaining HP after your run.

Unknown details: It’s still unclear whether this event is personal, server-wide, or cross-server. Stay tuned for confirmation when it goes live.

Why this matters: Progression mats for Mythic gear are time-gated by element days. If you don’t have depth in an element, your income is worse that day. Saturday/Sunday become catch-up windows.

Prep tips

  • Bench-build: Promote/star-up side-element Immortals so they can hold 3 skills even if you don’t dust them yet. Example: if you don’t main Water, star up Merlin so he can carry good gold skills on Mondays.
  • For instance, a Seondeok is awesome in PvE content, so get her star ranks done and use her during fire tuesdays!
  • Don’t blow stardust on off-march units yet; prioritize stars → skill slots.
  • Keep flexible gold skill pools to re-slot between elements.

4) Other Cap Increases

  • Resource points / Gnomes / Mech bosses / Lord Lv → all to 60.
  • Immortals: Lv60; Boost Level cap 35 (SP bottles matter again).
  • Dragons: Lv60; new talent nodes (expect both skill trees to reach Lv10 nodes).
  • Barracks: Higher-tier troops unlock.
  • Tower of Knowledge: New skills unlock with higher levels.
  • Academy: New Technologies; focus PvP stats first.
  • Well of Time & Elite dungeons: New chapters.
  • Fortification: Higher wall tiers.

Why this matters: It’s a total-stat jump across every layer. Expect arena/KVK DPS and tank checks to rise quickly once a few whales hit 35 boosts and Lv10 dragon nodes.

Prep tips

  • Hoard SP bottles and dragon crystals; those two are immediate, visible power spikes.
  • Save unclaimed daily/quest EXP on alts/mains if you were holding them—turn-in post-60 unlock to jump-start Lord levels.
  • Prioritize Academy lines that directly give Atk/Def/HP for your main march types.

Legendary Season – Structure & KVK Flow

Opening & Off-Season

  • Opens Oct 20, 00:00 UTC for servers that joined preview (S1–S232; M1–M12).
  • First off-season before the first Legendary KVK is extended to 30 days; later ones revert to 14 days.

Why this matters: You get a one-time month to climb the new caps before the first Legendary KVK. Plan your alliance’s upgrade sprint around this window.

Alliance Registration (Legion of Frostborne)

  • Registration/matchmaking/settlement are now Alliance-based.
  • Window: 72 hours after off-season opens.
  • Who registers: R6/R5 (manual). After deadline, the system can auto-assign alliances to factions based on active members and power.
  • Skip rule: Alliances that participated in the previous round can choose to skip the current one (not for brand-new/no-history alliances).
  • Alliance lock after the deadline: you’re bound to your alliance for that KVK. Leaving and coming back to the same alliance is okay; switching alliances or migrating blocks entry for that round. New joiners after the deadline cannot participate that round.

Why this matters: No more freewheeling alt alliance hopscotch mid-season. Leadership needs to coordinate who’s in before the deadline and avoid late swaps.

Migration Overhaul – Command Power & Slots

Command Power

Each server calculates daily at 00:00 UTC the average of top players’ historical highest power. That average is the server’s Command Power benchmark.

Special Migration Slots

  • If a player’s historical highest lord power ≥ Command Power of the target server, they must consume 1 Special Migration Slot from that server to move in. Otherwise, no slot needed.
  • Slot quantities by season:
    • Season 1: 3 per server
    • Season 2: 5 per server
    • Conquest: 8 per server
    • Legendary: 8 per server
  • Slots refresh when the server enters a new season.

King Settings

  • Allow Special Migration: High-power players (≥ Command Power) can enter by consuming slots; others free.
  • Disallow Special Migration: Blocks all players ≥ Command Power. Others free.
  • If there’s no King, the last saved King setting persists.

What this changes in practice

  • Kings become gatekeepers. Recruitment of whales is a strategic resource decision.
  • Scarcity: A tiny slot pool forces alliances to rank recruits and coordinate multi-player moves.
  • Season timing matters: Some groups will wait for a season change to refresh slots.

Server strategy notes

  • New S1/S2: Protects early ecosystems; only a handful of over-cap players can enter.
  • Conquest/Legendary: Still tight. Expect pre-arranged slot reservations and audits of candidate historical highest.

New Tower Skill – Fully Prepared

  • Type: Offensive Immortal only. Mutually exclusive with Counterattack (cannot equip both).
  • Effect: Each normal attack increases damage dealt by 1.8% + 0.6%/level and reduces damage taken by 1.5% + 0.5%/level, stacking up to 10 times.
  • Acquisition: Wisdom Well event.
  • Suggested users (from notes): Ares, Alexander, Hannibal, Wukong, Poseidon, etc.

How it plays

  • It’s a ramp skill keyed to basic attack cadence. On fast-hitting or extended fights, the stack cap yields notable DPS + survivability. On burst/short fights, it may underperform immediate-value skills.
  • Clashes with Counterattack builds—so choose between sustained ramp vs reactive damage loops.

Meta note: While this skill seems tuned to boost Ares, it could actually push Alexander back into meta relevance. With multiple attack speed-based skills now in circulation, Alex’s value in sustained DPS comps may surge again.

Quality-of-Life & Economy Tweaks

  • Forge conversion: Each converted item can be collected immediately; Gold requires at least 10,000 per collect. You can manually input conversion amounts now.
  • Alliance Help now works on Dragon upgrades (huge time saver post-55).
  • Battle Pass (Golden Path): Daily purchasable levels cap raised to 30 (applies next BP cycle after the update; missed days don’t roll over).
  • Daily Mission Lord EXP for Lv41–55 increased from 200 → 500.
  • Bug Fix: Iron Curtain no longer weakens enemies’ barriers if they have no barrier effects active (fixes unintended interactions).

Why this matters

  • Faster dragon timelines during Legendary sprint.
  • Early/mid accounts climb Lord levels faster, helping them reach 55/Legendary gating.
  • BP buyers can compress progress per day, but not retroactively.

Practical Day‑1 Plan (Oct 20 Legendary Unlock)

  1. Forge 55 check → Start Azure conversion loop.
  2. Academy → Queue first PvP-stat techs unlocked by 56–60 tiers, unless major dev. nodes are available. Look for Troop count and Crit Damage (unknown if added, what I will look for first once patch drops).
  3. Dragon → Upgrade + spam Alliance Help; aim for new Lv10 nodes quickly.
  4. Immortal boosts → Pump SP to your main carry line; aim Tier 34–35 on DPS first.
  5. Elemental Domain → Hit the day’s element with a pre-built bench; use weekend to make up weak elements.
  6. Gear → Push Legendary+ to 60 on your #1 DPS, then Mythic reforge; keep mats for rerolls.
  7. Alliance admin → Handle KVK registration within the 72h window; lock rosters early; communicate migration stance with the King.

Conclusion Summary

  • Legendary Season is a systems gate: Energy Cores, Elemental Domain, and Mythic reforges will pace your progress more than raw speedups.
  • Mythic gear + Immortal Tier 35 + Dragon Lv10 nodes are the big three power spikes. Plan mats and rerolls around your primary DPS.
  • Alliance/KVK becomes more administrative: registration windows, roster locks, and migration slots turn kingship into a strategic role.
  • Bottom line: Prep your Forge, hoard SP/dragon mats, build minimal element benches, and align your alliance on migration/KVK logistics before Oct 20.

Notes & Sources

patch-2-8-7.title: Patch 2.8.7 – Arthur nerf, more artifacts to the people and battle pass changes and more

patch-2-8-7.html:
Patch 2.8.7 dropped with a lot of hype around Wildfire Furnace and Alliance Supremacy. Those are cool new events and worth checking out in the official news posts, but the real long-term impact of this patch lies deeper in the notes. Some subtle changes here could shake up progression, the gem economy, and even the late-game meta. Let’s dig into the big ones.

Battle Pass Expansion & Shop

The Legendary & Peak Battle Pass has been expanded up to 100 levels, with levels now purchasable. On top of that, a Battle Pass Shop has been added where you can spend Inferno Insignia on Holy, Shadow, and Chaos immortal fragments plus their exclusive artifacts.

3. Legendary & Peak Battle Pass

1) Legendary & Peak Battle Pass levels increased to 100, with battle pass levels available for purchase.

2) Battle Pass shop opened, where Inferno Insignia can be used to purchase Holy, Shadow, and Chaos Immortal Fragments and their exclusive artifacts.

3) Inferno Insignia can be obtained through premium battle pass rewards, participating in Festival Events, purchasing festival packs, etc.

The way it works. Player Exe has been kind enough to share details with us:

  • Each BP level now gives 10 medallions.
  • It costs 450 medallions for 60 fragments (holy/shadow).
  • Buying a level costs 600 gems.

Basically, you can think of the mechanics to how this work as the normal GP, we have 50 levels of rewards and then we repeat level 50. But instead of an unlimited repeat of level 50 (like in normal GP) we have a cap of 100 levels, i.e. 50 levels that are just currency rewards. Basically a GP but capped at level 100 instead of unlimited.

Buying immortals this way is thus:

  • 27,000 gems = 60 frags of a Holy/Shadow immortal.

While gemming levels here for fragments is not particularly cheap, the path in itself with the 100 level version is incredibly good value. And even tho is is not cheap, and most players aren’t going to be spamming it, the upside is this adds another gem → useful fragments conversion path, which has been a theme in recent updates. Slow farming it with free pass levels is probably the most realistic play for most players, but whales now have a guaranteed gem sink for Shadow/Holy progress.

Completing the Battle Pass in the new version is super high value. For just 30$ you will get 2150 gems, 60 immortal fragment selection chests for holy/shadow, 1000 medallions (i.e. little over 120 frags) and 60 random holy/shadow fragments by completing daily quests consistently and maxing out the pass event. Comparatively, the old version yielded just 90 selection chests and 30 random holy/shadow fragments as you completed the 50 levels there.

Note, completing 100 levels should be doable without gemming since the quests have gotten an EXP buff. Player Exe who has been kind enough to share is past level 14 in 4 days without completing every quest.

Battle Pass Shop S2 Updates

The Monthly BP Shop S2 now includes Ragnar, Mehmed II, Toyotomi Hideyoshi, Darius, and Cao Cao fragments, along with their artifacts.

The notes say “Monthly Battle Pass Shop S2 season adds Ragnar, Mehmed II, Toyotomi Hideyoshi, Darius the Great, and Cao Cao fragments, along with exclusive artifacts.”

This is honestly a very welcome change. Ragnar and Cao Cao artifacts in particular have been high-demand pieces. A lot of players stalled out because you needed specific events to push those, so BP making them more accessible is a win.

And it ties nicely with the Sparks of Galaxy S2 update:

3) Sparks of Galaxy event S2 season adds seasonal Immortal exclusive artifact selection box.

The Seasonal Immortals tend to reference the ones available in e.g. Battle Pass as notes above, which is great. Now you can also grab seasonal Immortal exclusive artifact selection boxes in Galaxy! This is the same as the new seasonal addition in the Daily Pearl Shop, though that one is a bit expensive. Anyway, if you for example, is running a YSS + Himiko build (one of the strongest Season 2 metas), you can now farm Himiko artifacts within the same Galaxy event cycle. Much smoother progression for focused builds.

King Arthur Reflection Nerf

This one’s huge for late-game PvP.

Arthur’s reflection used to basically act like true damage. If you dropped him against an Apollo-heavy whale march, his reflect ignored their reduction stats — so Apollo just ate that damage raw. That made Arthur one of the few effective counters to big Apollo setups.

King Arthur Damage Reflection Algorithm Fix

After the fix, King Arthur’s reflected damage will be affected by the target’s damage reduction attributes.

Now:

  • Reflection does scale with the target’s damage reduction (YSS, Tower of Knowledge nodes, artifact reductions, etc.).
  • In practice, this means Arthur is going to bounce back much less damage to whales, since stacked defensive stats will blunt it.

I’ll be real — this probably kills his role as a “budget whale counter.” Without that cheese, he may slide back into obscurity unless something else keeps him relevant. Which is a shame, because he offered a very different tool compared to the standard bruisers. I hope the devs keep tweaking him instead of letting him rot.

If you’re mid-game and thinking of building him now, I’d wait to see how the meta reacts. He might still be okay for general marches, but his days of cracking Apollo are gone.

Other Small but Notable Changes

  • Immortal Specialization Master All: being able to preset and instantly unlock entire node chains is a nice QoL upgrade. Less clicking, more experimenting.
  • Daily Deals Shop: Holy and Shadow artifacts after 75 days → great for newer servers catching up.
  • Training Grounds raid requirement lowered: from 30% reserves to 10%. Means you can raid more aggressively without gimping your training, which is solid for active servers.
  • Gem auto removal: if you’ve ever had to unsocket multiple gems from one piece, you’ll love this.

Player Perspective

If I had to break it down:

  • Battle Pass changes are the best part of this patch for long-term growth. Even if you don’t whale, just having the option to slowly gem → fragment farm is progress.
  • Galaxy S2 + BP Shop updates smooth out a lot of the artifact bottlenecks. This is going to speed up how fast people can actually finish their intended builds.
  • Arthur fix is the one sore spot. It makes sense for balance, but it also cuts away one of the only fun curveballs against top-tier Apollo whales.

If it were me, I’d be putting gems into the BP shop path as a long-term holy/shadow investment, while holding off on Arthur until we see if he survives in the new balance landscape.

Bottom Line

Patch 2.8.7 is sneaky important. Everyone’s eyes are on Wildfire and Alliance Supremacy, but the Battle Pass overhaul and Arthur nerf will affect the actual day-to-day progression and PvP scene way more.

  • More ways to farm Shadow/Holy = win.
  • Easier access to artifacts = win.
  • Arthur losing his cheese = probably a loss, unless you never built him in the first place.

So, my advice? Start planning how to use gems in the new BP shop, enjoy the smoother artifact paths, and keep an eye on how the PvP tier list shifts without Arthur as a counterpick.

Published: 14-09-2025

patch-2-8-6.description: Patch 2.8.6 is here, bringing substantial changes to Infinity Kingdom’s core mechanics and introducing exciting new features. As always, I’ll unpack all the details, explain their impact, and share what this means for your game experience and strategy. Whether you’re a casual player or a competitive
patch-2-8-6.html:
📌 Main Points from Patch 2.8.6 (TL;DR)

  • New Hybrid Meta Skill:
    The introduction of Knife Through Butter will revitalize Hybrid setups. With its rapid energy drain, this skill is set to disrupt the current hyper-regen meta by preventing enemy immortals from casting ultimates as frequently. Expect high-speed Hybrid teams using Wind Rage and Berserker to become popular again.
  • No More Endless Gemming of Prosperity:
    The update introduces scaling gem costs for restoring Prosperity, making repeated gemming increasingly costly each day. This change encourages smarter and more strategic PvP play, emphasizing careful planning over limitless gem-spending.
  • Holy Team Buff – Manco Cápac vs. Confuse:
    Manco Cápac now grants Holy Immortals Control Immunity, specifically countering problematic Confuse skills used by immortals like Tomyris and Loki. This provides Holy teams a powerful defensive advantage against crowd control, enhancing their viability in the PvP meta.

Comprehensive Guide to Patch 2.8.6 – Infinity Kingdom’s Latest Update Explained

Patch 2.8.6 is here, bringing substantial changes to Infinity Kingdom’s core mechanics and introducing exciting new features. As always, I’ll unpack all the details, explain their impact, and share what this means for your game experience and strategy. Whether you’re a casual player or a competitive strategist, this update brings something significant for everyone.

🔥 Key Highlights of Patch 2.8.6:

This update introduces several major additions and adjustments, each designed to balance gameplay, add strategic depth, and improve your overall gaming experience.

⚔️ 1. New Pinnacle Trial Ranking System

The Pinnacle Trial now features a competitive ranking system, called Trial Ranking. Here’s how it works:

  • Points System: Players clearing the Pinnacle Trial stages earn ranking points. Top 10 scorers appear on the leaderboard.
  • Challenges: You can challenge players on the leaderboard. Winning earns you ranking points; losing has no penalty.
  • Limited Attempts: Daily challenge attempts are limited, so make them count.
  • Ranking Rewards: End-of-event rewards scale based on your final rank, providing extra incentive for competitive play.

What it Means for You:
This adds a welcome competitive edge to PvE gameplay, making Pinnacle Trials more rewarding and engaging. Players with strong PvE setups can now shine even brighter and earn well-deserved bragging rights and rewards.

📚 2. New Tower of Knowledge Skills

🗡️ Knife Through Butter (Legendary Skill)

  • Effect: After every 6 normal attacks, deal AoE physical damage (60% + 20%/level) with a 60% chance to drain enemy energy by 90 + 30/level.
  • Acquisition: Available via Wisdom Well during Conquest Season.

Strategic Impact:
A game-changer, especially for Hybrid setups. With high attack-speed Immortals, this skill dramatically disrupts enemy ultimates. It directly counters the current hyper-regen meta by consistently draining enemy energy.

🛡️ Iron Curtain (Epic Skill)

  • Effect: Normal attacks have a chance (18% + 6%/level) to weaken enemy barriers by 30% for 3 seconds. Also grants a damage reduction buff (10.5% + 3.5%/level) when troop strength is above 70%.
  • Acquisition: Available via Conquest Season Recharge Gifts Pack.

Strategic Impact:
Useful for tankier frontlines and teams facing barrier-heavy opponents. The added defensive buff further improves sustain, making it great for tanky setups and bruisers.

⚖️ 3. Optimizations & Adjustments

📌 Wisdom Well Event Shop Improvements

The following valuable skills are now more easily accessible:

  • S1 Skills: Fire of Rage, Victorious Pursuit, Snipe, Stormeye, Curse of Pain, Blade Vortex, Toxin Barrier, Demonic Contract, Void Realm.
  • Conquest Season Skills: Siren’s Gaze, Weakness Protection, Berserker, Wind Rage.

Player Impact:
This broadens strategic diversity, allowing players easier access to skills previously challenging to obtain. Expect richer and more varied team compositions.

💎 Prosperity Gem Cost Changes

To curb endless gem-spending on Prosperity recovery (a common frustration in PvP):

  • Gem cost for restoring Prosperity now scales upward with each daily use.
  • Costs reset at UTC 0:00 daily.

Strategic Impact:
Players now need to think carefully before gemming prosperity repeatedly. It promotes smarter gameplay, requiring thoughtful engagement and strategic resource management.

🌎 Migration Power Cap Increased

  • The King’s migration power cap is now raised significantly (from 2-3 million to 4-6 million power) based on completed Contention of Relics battles.

Player Impact:
This change enables stronger players to migrate between servers, fostering greater competitiveness and flexibility for seasoned players or alliances looking to merge or recruit high-power lords.

🛒 Golden Path Shop Display Update

  • Now clearly displays item quantities, improving clarity and ease of shopping.

🎯 Balance Adjustments to Immortals

Several Immortals received significant balance tweaks, increasing their viability:

🔸 Manco Cápac

  • Now grants Control Immunity to all Holy Immortals and increases Dodge Rate for 15 seconds.
  • Becomes immune to Confuse after casting, periodically dealing Physical Damage afterward, but no longer gains energy post-cast.

Impact: Significantly improves Holy team defense against crowd-control, enhancing sustained battles.

🔸 Khubilai Khan

  • Damage increased slightly (now 78% + 26%/level) on wolf attacks.
  • Each wolf has a 60% chance to apply stacking debuffs, increasing the target’s physical damage received (up to 3 stacks).

Impact: Strengthens Khan’s viability, especially in physical-damage-focused teams, making him a more attractive frontline DPS/support hybrid.

🔸 Nebuchadnezzar II

  • Base Energy Regen Speed significantly increased (66 → 83 points/second).

Impact: Faster ultimate casts will improve his utility, potentially shifting builds around Nebuchadnezzar II and enhancing his usage in competitive teams.

📌 Strategic Analysis: What Does This Patch Mean for You?

Patch 2.8.6 clearly aims at game balance:

  • Hybrid setups return strongly to the meta, challenging dominant pure magic and hyper-regen teams.
  • The new Prosperity gem cost scaling forces strategic resource management, reducing “infinite shielding” and encouraging tactical decision-making.
  • Improved skill availability in Wisdom Well greatly enhances player flexibility, letting you experiment with builds you might previously have overlooked.
  • Improved migration flexibility offers strategic options for highly competitive players or alliances.

This patch makes strategic planning, thoughtful investment, and tactical flexibility more important than ever.

🔮 Predictions: What’s Next in the Meta?

I predict significant shifts in the meta following Patch 2.8.6:

  • Hybrid setups (physical/magical mixed teams) will see a strong resurgence.
  • Skills promoting high attack speed (Wind Rage, Berserker) and energy disruption (Knife Through Butter) will dominate the new strategic landscape.
  • Prosperity gem cost changes will promote smarter PvP engagement, rewarding more strategic and calculated players.

📖 Conclusion & TL;DR

Patch 2.8.6 offers a mix of new strategic depth, balancing adjustments, and quality-of-life improvements, emphasizing thoughtful gameplay:

  • New Pinnacle Trial rankings add competitive PvE depth.
  • Knife Through Butter and Iron Curtain skills provide crucial meta shifts, reviving hybrid strategies.
  • Prosperity gem scaling encourages smarter PvP play.
  • Easier skill access from Wisdom Well diversifies build options.
  • Increased migration power cap enhances server competitiveness.

In short, Infinity Kingdom Patch 2.8.6 significantly changes how we approach team-building, PvP strategy, and PvE challenges. Adaptation and careful planning are now keys to victory.
